screening_results.reason: The study reports fMRI in humans performing a Wheel of Fortune task that manipulates risk and ambiguity (decision-making under risk and ambiguity). It includes within-task contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (Risk Gamble > Ambiguity Gamble and Ambiguity Gamble > Risk Gamble) and outcome contrasts (Gain > No Gain), satisfying condition-vs-condition criteria. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain second-level GLMs with voxelwise/cluster inference and reported peak coordinates (tables), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are healthy adolescents (acceptable participant group). Reporting of coordinates and thresholds is present. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not against implicit baseline only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This fMRI study investigates risky and ambiguous decision-making during a gambling task and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (meets I4 and I5). However, the NeuroStore extract shows the reported analysis is a region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding) with reported peaks only within predefined ROIs and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. Therefore it does not meet I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Participants and task otherwise acceptable (I7). Full text is available in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study uses an intertemporal (delay-discounting) choice task manipulating time-ambiguity rather than a risky, ambiguous (as defined by the review), or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criterion E5 explicitly excludes delay discounting / intertemporal choice tasks. The paper does meet several inclusion criteria: it reports an ambiguity > exact contrast (Amb > Ex) and condition contrasts (I5), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I8). However I4 (task is a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review) is not met because the task is intertemporal delay discounting, triggering E5. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study used fMRI during a decision-making task contrasting ambiguity vs risk (meets I4 and I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates (meets I6 and I8) and includes an eligible participant group (I7). However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (ambiguity>risk between-group and a group-by-condition interaction) and does not report any unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects. Because the paper reports only between-group contrasts with no accompanying within-group whole-brain task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E8 and must be excluded.

The paper reports an fMRI (BOLD) study of ambiguous decision-making (second-order uncertainty) in human participants (n=20) and includes within-group contrasts comparing ambiguous vs nonambiguous gambles and parametric modulation of second-order uncertainty. Crucially, Analysis 21451019_analysis_0 is a group-level (second-level random effects) whole-brain voxelwise analysis with FWE-corrected inference, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during relevant decision-making), I5 (decision-making contrasts: ambiguous > nonambiguous and parametric uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain evidence), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study used fMRI in human participants and reports an ambiguity contrast (ambiguity > ignorance) at group level (one-sample t-test) with coordinates reported, so it meets I4, I5, I7, and I8. However, although the model was fit over the whole brain, statistical inference was restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume FWE correction (ROI-only inference), meaning no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked results are reported. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI results reported). Therefore the paper is excluded.

This study reports fMRI in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making gambling task (play vs pass) with a within-group contrast Play > Pass, which corresponds to a risky>safe decision-making comparison. The analysis was a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression with inference over the whole brain (FWE-corrected), and coordinates/peaks are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI/connectivity, not baseline-only contrasts).

This fMRI study reports within-task contrasts of risky decision-making (e.g., risk > delay; riskier option > safer option) collected during human participants performing monetary gamble choices. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate peaks (tables). Although the task also includes intertemporal choices, the paper provides clear risky-DM contrasts meeting the review’s risky decision-making definitions. All required inclusion criteria are met (fMRI during risky decision task; at least one relevant decision-versus-decision contrast; whole-brain group-level results; acceptable participant group; results reported as coordinate peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not resting/connectivity-only, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record. Hence INCLUDE.

This study reports fMRI in humans performing two risky decision-making tasks (Angling Risk Task and Balloon Analog Risk Task) with within-group contrasts of decision events (e.g., Risky choice, Cash-out, Loss) and direct paired-task contrasts (ART > BART and BART > ART). Model estimation and inference were performed at the whole-brain voxel level and results are reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults (n=23). Thus the study meets inclusion I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition-vs-condition and between-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline).

This study reports task-based fMRI during risky and ambiguous decision-making (I4). It includes within-task condition contrasts comparing decision conditions (Risk > Ambiguity; Dangerous > Safe), satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts (I5). The reported results are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding information (FWE-corrected; whole-brain inference), meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting standards (I6, I8). Participants are healthy adolescents and young adults (acceptable per I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not against implicit baseline (E3), the modality is fMRI not PET (E4), the task targets risky/ambiguous decision-making rather than excluded task types (E5), whole-brain results are reported rather than ROI-only (E6), and it is an empirical task-activation study (not E7, E8, or E9). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, so it should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a gambling (risky/ambiguous decision-making) task and includes direct condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to the review (e.g., decision-making under risk > decision-making under ambiguity; bet choices > safe choices). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM maps with reported coordinate peaks (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Both within-group contrasts (controls and patients) and between-group interactions are presented. The task and contrasts match the meta-analysis definitions for risky and ambiguous decision-making. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria.

Excluded under E8: The NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (CUD > controls and controls > CUD) comparing groups across decision conditions, with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects (e.g., risky>safe or other within-task decision-making contrasts) reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task decision-making contrast or decision-vs-control contrast reported in the record). Because the study reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect, it must be excluded per E8.

Excluded because the reported analyses are region-of-interest only: model fitting and inference were restricted to ROIs with small-volume correction (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). This meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — Wheel of Fortune), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions: high-risk>low-risk, 25/75>50/50, 25/75>control), I7 (participant group acceptable — adolescents), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study reports event-related fMRI in healthy humans performing the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task (I4). It includes within-group contrasts that meet the required forms: task>control (monetary > monochromatic control) and risky>safe (high reward/risk > low reward/risk) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Analyses 15327927_analysis_0, _1, and _4: model fit and inference over whole brain, voxel-level p<0.001), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participants and reporting are acceptable (I7, I8). ROI analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI of humans performing a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and includes a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast risky > safe (Analysis 20302946_analysis_0: whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, one-sample t-test). This satisfies I4 (fMRI risky task), I5 (risky > safe contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I7 (participant group acceptable) and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, does not report only ROIs (it includes a whole-brain analysis), does not use only baseline contrasts, and is empirical. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record representation (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study used fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (an ambiguous decision-making task), so I4 is satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record shows the reported analysis is an ROI-based (vmPFC) correlation (wins > losses correlated with BIS-11NP) with 'Model fit over: region of interest' and only one reported peak. Inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) is not met because results are limited to an ROI. The contrast provided (wins > losses) indexes outcome evaluation rather than one of the meta-analysis’s required decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguity high>low or task>control), so I5 is not satisfied as reported. Therefore the paper must be excluded under E6 (ROI-only results). No indication the full text was incomplete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (visual categorization, audio-visual synchrony, random-dot motion). It reports within-group contrasts that match perceptual-DM definitions (degraded/noisy > clear; low-coherence (12%,20%) > 100% coherence), i.e., hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps were estimated and reported (one-sample t-tests; whole-brain inference; FWE-corrected thresholds; reported peak coordinates). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a risky decision-making task with explicit probabilities and incentives (dice arrangements, potential gains/losses), meeting I4. It reports within-task contrasts (A>B and A>C) comparing decision conditions, satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects second-level t-tests with corrected thresholding and reported peak coordinates, meeting I6 and I8. Participants are human (healthy older adults), which is acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is fMRI (not PET), provides condition-versus-condition contrasts (not task>rest only), reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and is empirical. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports an fMRI task of probabilistic (uncertain) decision-making (lake reasoning) performed by human participants (I4). It includes a decision-task versus active control contrast (lake reasoning > color naming) satisfying the required task-vs-control form (I5). Importantly, the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps with FWE-corrected results (Analyses 24831391_analysis_2 and _3: whole-brain model fit and inference), fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I6). Participant groups include schizophrenia patients and healthy controls, which are acceptable (I7). Results are reported as peaks/tables (coordinates), meeting reporting requirements (I8). Although some ROI (small-volume) analyses are present (Analyses 0 and 1), the presence of whole-brain, group-level task contrasts means the study is not excluded under E6. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a probabilistic decision-making task (jumping-to-conclusions paradigm) and includes contrasts comparing decision-making to an active control (lake decision > colour decision) and within-task contrasts (last fish > previous), satisfying the decision-making task requirement. Crucially, whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses are reported (Analyses 4 and 5: whole-brain, FWE-corrected, 1-sample t tests with reported peak tables), so whole-brain evidence is available. Participant groups (ARMS patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. Results are reported in tables of peaks. Although several ROI-restricted analyses are present, they do not preclude inclusion because unmasked whole-brain maps are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI without whole-brain, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8.

This is an fMRI study (n=17) in which participants performed a multi-armed bandit decision-making task manipulating uncertainty/risk. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects GLM analyses with parametric modulation contrasts for risk, estimation uncertainty, unexpected uncertainty, and learning rate (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain in multiple analyses). These contrasts constitute within-task decision-making comparisons (parametric high vs low uncertainty/risk effects), meeting the meta-analysis definition for risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts. Results are reported in standard coordinate space (MNI) with cluster-level correction, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not ROI-only, not task>baseline-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a gambling (risk) task and reports contrasts comparing gamble-choice vs certainty-choice (risky vs certain), satisfying the decision-making contrast requirement. Analyses are group-level (one-sample t-tests) with searchlight MVPA fit across the brain and inference reported over the whole brain with cluster-level thresholding and peak coordinates, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Participants are healthy humans (n=14). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are condition-vs-condition rather than baseline). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI study (bold response) of human participants performing a gambling decision-making task manipulating risk, ambiguity, and sample-space ignorance. It contains within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., ambiguity > risk; SSI > risk; ambiguity & SSI > risk), satisfying the required contrast forms for ambiguous- and risky-DM. Analyses were fit over the whole brain at the group level (mixed-effects group analysis) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants (n=38, adults) are acceptable. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables of peaks is allowed. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and should be included.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI perceptual decision-making study with whole-brain, group-level GLM results (n=32). However, the reported task contrasts are condition > rest for each of the four conditions (happy clear; happy noisy; angry clear; angry noisy > rest). No condition-versus-condition contrast (e.g., hard > easy, noisy > clear) or task > active control contrast is reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E3 (only task>rest contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain map), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (results reported in extractable form). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-condition vs decision-condition or task>control contrast).

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (facial emotion discrimination) and reports a contrast comparing ambiguous > easy trials, so it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (decision-condition contrast), and I7 (healthy participants). However, the reported analysis shows the model was fit over the whole brain but inference was restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (ROI SVC) and the provided contrast is an interaction/between-group contrast. The document reports only ROI-inference peaks for a between-group interaction and does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map. Therefore it fails to provide the required whole-brain group-level statistical map (I6 not met) and meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI results/no whole-brain results) and E8 (reports only a between-group/interaction contrast with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect).

This study examined fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains) with healthy adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (cluster-thresholded) comparing decision conditions. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (contrasts involving risky vs safe/feedback conditions), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), I8 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). However, all reported analyses are between-group sex contrasts/interactions (Females > Males) and no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., risky > safe within subjects) are presented in the extracted record. Per exclusion criterion E8, studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect must be excluded. Therefore exclude under E8. Inclusion criteria not met for the purpose of pooling (no within-group task effect available for inclusion as a task activation contrast).

Although the study used fMRI on human participants performing risky (probabilistic) and intertemporal choices and reports whole-brain voxelwise modeling, it does not report an admissible risk-related contrast as required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or task > control). The reported analyses are parametric modulations (correlations with subjective value) and two ROI-restricted inferences for value correlations; the PD-specific analysis is ROI-restricted and the whole-brain result is a conjunction/uncorrected map of value correlations rather than a condition-versus-condition or task-versus-control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky/probabilistic decision-making present), I6 (group-level whole-brain modeling reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no eligible condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

This is an fMRI study (n=24 healthy adults) of financial decision-making under risk, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (MESSAGE vs NO MESSAGE; FOLLOWED vs IGNORED) and parametric modulators of lottery value and sure-win magnitude, all tested with random-effects/group-level whole-brain models and reported peak coordinates. These contrasts are condition-versus-condition decision-making comparisons (not task>baseline) and therefore meet the review’s requirements for risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not non-empirical).

The study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (model fit and inference restricted to ROI) with region-level thresholding and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. This violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous decision-making gambling task), I5 (within-task contrasts parametric for ambiguity/conflict), and I7 (eligible participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results) and I8 (not applicable because no whole-brain results reported). Full text is complete for screening.

This single-case fMRI study directly assesses decision making under risk and ambiguity using a dice-based task and reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (A > B) comparing two decision-making conditions, meeting the contrast requirement. Whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported for A>B pre and post (voxel-level, p<0.05) with peak coordinates (Table 3), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are human patients (n=1); the review accepts any participant groups. Coordinates are reported in tables, consistent with acceptable reporting. Some analyses used ROI SVC, but whole-brain within-task results are present. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (I4) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (I6) with coordinate tables (I8), and the participant sample is acceptable (I7), the NeuroStore record does not report any contrast that directly compares two decision-making conditions (e.g., high-risk > low-risk) or a decision-making task versus an active control task. The reported analyses are parametric regressions and modulations tied to prediction errors and individual differences (difference of weights), but no explicit task-versus-task contrast matching the inclusion examples (I5) is provided. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text is complete as provided.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI study in which participants performed a gambling task with explicit risk parameters (potential gain, potential loss, outcome probability) and the authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects one-sample t-test maps for multiple decision-related parametric contrasts (expected value, probability, variance, potential gain/loss). This satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (results reported as peak coordinates in tables), and I5 (within-task decision-related contrasts via parametric modulators representing risky decision variables). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not only between-group). Full text representation appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

The study reports human fMRI during an ambiguous/risky decision-making task (I4). It includes a within-group contrast directly comparing ambiguous vs risky choices (choice under ambiguity > choice under risk), which matches admissible ambiguous-DM contrasts (I5). The reported analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise models with whole-brain inference and coordinate peaks (Model fit and Inference over: whole brain; reported peaks), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6 and I8). Participant sample is reported and acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI BART (risky decision-making) experiment and a contrast reflecting experimental block > control block, but the reported analyses are region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it does not provide the required group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses reported) and E8 (only a between-group interaction contrast reported with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect apparent). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (contrast compares experimental vs control block for decision-making), I7 (healthy participants acceptable), I8 (peaks/coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain evidence). Because I6 is required, the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI BOLD during a risky/ambiguous decision task (Wheel of Fortune) in human participants (I4); it reports within-task contrasts and comparisons of decision conditions including SV risk, SV ambiguity, and SV risk > SV ambiguity (I5); group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates are provided (I6, I8); participants are an eligible human sample (adolescents; I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the analyses are not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7), not contrasts vs implicit baseline only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E8), and this is empirical fMRI data (not E9). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (HC risk-disadvantageous > IGD risk-advantageous) at the group level with whole-brain coordinate peaks. Although the study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (I4) and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (I5), provides whole-brain group-level results in MNI coordinates (I6, I8), and participants are eligible (I7), the extracted contrasts are exclusively between-group/interactions with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect reported. This meets exclusion criterion E8 (studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI meta-analysis of ambiguous decision-making. I4: fMRI was conducted while human participants performed an ambiguity/uncertainty decision task (decide to land or abort under high vs low uncertainty). I5: The paper reports within-task condition contrasts relevant to ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty; financial vs neutral). I6: The model was fit over the whole brain and a group-level whole-brain contrast is reported (Neutral High vs implicit baseline; FDR-corrected whole-brain results and reported peak coordinates). I7: Participant group is healthy human adults. I8: Whole-brain results/peaks are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on implicit-baseline contrasts (it includes condition-versus-condition contrasts), is fMRI (not PET), includes ambiguity DM, and provides whole-brain results (not ROI-only). Therefore the paper should be included.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI study in human participants (n=14) performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney-face detection) with event-related RFX-GLM whole-brain analyses. Multiple within-task contrasts directly compare decision-related conditions versus stimulus/sensory conditions (e.g., Decision color/Decision response > Stimulus and vice versa), fulfilling the requirement for condition-versus-condition decision-making contrasts in a perceptual decision task. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain and reported voxelwise peaks (tables of coordinates) with voxel-level thresholding (p<0.01). This satisfies all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain contrasts).

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: (I4) fMRI was conducted while participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a decision-making task under ambiguity/risk); (I5) it reports within-group contrasts of decision-making > control conditions (decision-making task versus an active control); (I6) analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates; (I7) participant groups (newly diagnosed T2DM patients and matched healthy controls) are acceptable; (I8) whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are triggered: contrasts are versus an active control (not implicit baseline) so E3 does not apply; this is fMRI (not PET) so E4 does not apply; the task is a risky/ambiguous decision task (not an excluded task) so E5 does not apply; whole-brain results are provided so E6/E7 do not apply; within-group effects are reported so E8 does not apply. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task and reports parametric RPE effects and group interactions focusing on developmental differences in reward prediction error processing, not contrasts that map onto the review's risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Furthermore, the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (RPE parametric modulation and group × RPE interaction) with no unmasked within-group whole-brain task effect. Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task/contrast) and E8 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group whole-brain map) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain results reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/figures is acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM as defined by the review), I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast of the admissible forms).

Exclusion E8 applies: the NeuroStore record shows the reported contrasts are interaction/between-group comparisons only (group × condition interactions) with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task, ambiguous DM), I5 (within-task condition contrasts reported such as advantageous vs disadvantageous and wins vs losses), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported for some contrasts — analyses 1 and 3), I7 (participant groups acceptable — adolescents including clinical groups), I8 (results reported as peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied). Given E8, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a gambling (risky decision-making) task with an explicit within-group contrast comparing high-risk > low-risk (Analysis 15795134_analysis_0). The model was fit over the whole brain at the group level (one-sample t test) and reported voxelwise results (thresholds and coordinate peaks), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are human and within eligible ages. Results are reported in tables. Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity analyses, it includes an unmasked, whole-brain task activation contrast, so it does not meet exclusion E7. All required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Included for meta-analysis of risky decision-making contrasts.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risk-taking decision-making task and tests condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky > safe; risky > punished). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Talairach coordinates, cluster-level corrected via Monte-Carlo simulations) and results are presented as coordinate tables. Therefore it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not task>baseline only, modality is fMRI (not PET), results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), and the study reports within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: []. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using risky decision-making tasks (Iowa Gambling Task and a Risk Decision Task) with healthy human participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric GLM of reward/risk prediction and prediction errors) and reports coordinate peaks; thresholding is whole-brain FWE/cluster-level. Reported contrasts include conjunctions of within-task PE effects across IGT and RDT and a direct contrast IGT > RDT (between-task), which are admissible forms of decision-making contrasts. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are not task>baseline only, modality is fMRI not PET, tasks are risky decision-making, results are whole-brain rather than ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and the study provides within-task maps (conjunction) as well as between-task contrasts. Full text appears available in the record.

This study reports an fMRI investigation using the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task (I4). It provides condition-vs-condition contrasts including Risky > Safe and other within-task comparisons (I5). Models were fit over the whole brain and report group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results with reported peak coordinates (I6, I8). Participant groups (adolescents with/without family history) are acceptable (I7). Although some between-group contrasts used ROI-restricted inference, the paper also reports unmasked whole-brain within-group contrasts (e.g., risky vs safe within FHP and FHN and within healthy participants), so it meets the whole-brain evidence requirement and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Peaks and thresholding are reported in tables, satisfying reporting requirements. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI risky decision-making task (Simulated Driving Task) in human adolescents and includes within-subject contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (e.g., Go > Stop and Stop > Go), which map onto risky>safe comparisons. Analyses were fit over the whole brain and report group-level (random-effects) whole-brain results with peak coordinates in tables. Although the paper also reports seed-based PPI connectivity, it additionally provides whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts. Participants are human and eligible. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports human fMRI collected while subjects performed a perceptual decision task (random-dot-motion) combined with risky choice between performance-contingent lotteries, directly addressing risky/perceptual decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) mixed-effects analyses are reported with whole-brain inference and thresholding, and activation peaks are provided (coordinate table). Relevant contrasts include parametric condition contrasts of expected value/probability (e.g., EV C–EV NC, EV L2–EV L1), which constitute condition-versus-condition decision-making effects rather than task>baseline. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during relevant task), I5 (decision-related contrasts between conditions/parametric comparisons), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI study in human participants (n=13) performing a probabilistic reward-based decision task (sampling sides to maximize winnings), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group parametric-modulation contrasts (EV, RM, variance, TD prediction error) which are within-task decision-making contrasts acceptable per I5. Several analyses report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain inference (e.g., analyses 4, 10, 11, 12), meeting I6; whole-brain peaks are reported, satisfying I8. Participant sample is healthy humans within eligible age ranges, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a simulated driving task that operationalizes risky decision-making (Go vs Stop) in human adolescents. It includes within-subject condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Go > Stop, Pass > Crash) that directly compare decision-making conditions rather than task vs baseline. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported as peak coordinates (FWE-corrected voxelwise results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy humans (adolescents), which is an eligible sample. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The task is an in-scanner choice task requiring participants to choose a pronoun referent with manipulations of determinacy/uncertainty (Directly Determined, Indirectly Determined, Undetermined (Gender-Biased/Neutral)). Multiple contrasts compare ambiguous/undetermined conditions to directly determined conditions (e.g., Undetermined > Directly Determined) and a parametric modulation of uncertainty is reported, matching the meta-analysis contrast types for ambiguous decision-making (ambiguous > non-ambiguous; high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (second-level random effects, voxelwise inference) with reported coordinate peaks/tables. Participants are healthy humans (n=16). Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI experiment (n=16) in which participants performed a perceptual judgment task and BOLD patterns were related to decision variables (combined value and variability). This satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making). The reported contrasts (within-group parametric effects for 'variability' and 'combined value', including a variability regressor with and without RT) constitute within-task decision-related contrasts analogous to difficulty/uncertainty contrasts (e.g., hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence), meeting I5. Analyses were searchlight-based, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) inference with cluster-level correction and reported MNI peaks, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults, so I7 is also met. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only, and it reports within-group whole-brain task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) (I4). The reported primary contrast is switch > stay, a within-task decision-making condition comparison (I5). A group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported (analysis 26510167_analysis_0: model fit and inference over whole brain) with thresholding and reported peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participants (healthy adults) are an eligible group (I7). The whole-brain results are reported in tables/peaks consistent with allowed reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not baseline), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study used fMRI with human participants performing a risky choice task (I4 met) and reports group-level analyses and coordinate/ROI reporting practices (I8 met). Participants are an eligible group (I7 met). However, the NeuroStore extraction lists only contrasts comparing conditioned stimuli (Touched_CS > Shocked_CS and the reverse) and an ROI-based cross-subject regression in vmPFC. No contrast is reported that directly compares decision-making conditions of interest (e.g., risky > safe or risk > certainty), so inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. Additionally, there is no reported whole-brain, group-level decision-related (risk-related) statistical map (the decision-related reported analysis is ROI-only), so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 and I6 are not met, the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI (Iowa Gambling Task) in human participants and examines risk-related processes (risk prediction, reward prediction, choice difficulty) with parametric within-task contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise GLM, one-sample t-test) with whole-brain inference and coordinates reported (Talairach, peaks in Table 2). These meet the review’s requirements for risky decision-making, within-task contrasts, whole-brain evidence, acceptable participant sample, and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not task>rest only, not ROI-only, not PET, not solely connectivity or between-group-only effects. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

Study uses fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task), reports condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risk processing (active choice > passive no-choice; win > loss; risk-related contrasts noted), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level inference. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and this is empirical within-subject fMRI task activation data. Full text is complete in the provided record.

This study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task (stocks vs bonds) with whole-brain, random-effects analyses and decision-related contrasts (e.g., next bond > next stock). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (decision-making contrasts present), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates). However, all reported contrasts in the NeuroStore extraction are between-group comparisons and group × choice interactions (e.g., HC > EHO; EHE > HC; interactions next bond > next stock), and no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., risky > safe within HC or patients) are listed. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group whole-brain task effect) and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I4–I8 are met). Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a risky decision-making task and reports within-subject, whole-brain, group-level contrasts directly relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., 'Risky Choices > Safe Choices'). Analyses are second-level voxelwise GLMs with whole-brain inference and coordinate peaks reported. Participants are healthy humans (n=29). The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (task is risky DM, contains a risky > safe contrast, reports whole-brain group-level results, participant sample acceptable, and coordinates are reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reward-based decision task (probabilistic object reversal/virtual search for rewarding letters), with within-task contrasts comparing learning/search stages (e.g., Decision making > search; Reward processing > search). These are condition-versus-condition contrasts that index decision making under uncertainty (ambiguous/probabilistic decisions). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample and two-sample t-tests; whole-brain model fit; reported peak coordinates). Within-group task effects are present (young and old), and between-group comparisons are also reported. Therefore criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study (n=23) in which participants performed a perceptual decision/discrimination task (face vs house) during scanning (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects contrasts (report > follow and follow > report) with cluster-level FWE thresholding and tables of peak coordinates (satisfies I6 and I8). The report>follow contrast compares an active metacognitive report condition to a matched control (follow) within the perceptual decision task, meeting the requirement for a decision-task vs active control / within-task decision contrast (I5). Participant sample is acceptable per inclusion rules (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to implicit baseline contrasts (E3), not PET (E4), task is perceptual (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (E6 not met), and connectivity/ROI analyses do not constitute the only reported whole-brain task activation (E7 not met).

The study reports an fMRI investigation (BOLD) of the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) collected in humans (n=75 with AUD). It includes within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Mean Color Pumps > Mean White Pumps; Linear Color Pumps > Linear White Pumps; Explosion > Cashout), satisfying the requirement for decision-making contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise models and whole-brain inference are reported (peaks/tables provided) for several contrasts, and additional associations use whole-brain/ROI-restricted analyses; results are reported as tables of peaks. Participant group (AUD) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline-only, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI risky decision-making and reports contrasts between decision conditions (meets I4 and I5) in a healthy adult sample (meets I7). However, all reported statistical inferences are based on small-volume (ROI) corrections (FWE/FDR SVC) with inference restricted to regions of interest; no group-level whole-brain corrected task-evoked statistical maps are reported. Therefore it fails to provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (I6 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI-based inference reported).

The study reports fMRI data collected while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making) and presents multiple within-task contrasts that compare different decision conditions (parametric modulation by pump number during pumping and cash-out, and a direct contrast: pumping following an explosion > pumping following a cash out). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates. Although PET was used on a subset for receptor binding, the primary reported task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results meet inclusion and do not make the study a PET-only paper. All applicable inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text is available in the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task in human participants (healthy adults) and includes a within-group risky > safe contrast (selecting 40/80 > selecting 20), satisfying the risky-DM contrast requirement. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with inference over the whole brain and peaks reported in Table 2, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. Participants and task fit the review scope. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) in human participants (n=14) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. It includes within-task contrasts and parametric modulation of risk (e.g., activations covaried with voluntary/involuntary risk) and condition contrasts (active choice > passive no-choice), reported with voxelwise inference (FDR-corrected) and peak tables. These meet the review’s requirements for an fMRI risky-DM task, condition-vs-condition contrasts, whole-brain group-level maps, acceptable participant sample, and acceptable reporting format. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply.

The study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task (overturned-cup risky choices) and includes at least one decision-making contrast (risky choice > nonrisky choice). Analyses were conducted voxelwise across the whole brain with whole-brain inference and report peak coordinates (tables), fulfilling the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participant sample (anxious youth and controls) is an acceptable population, and results are reported in coordinate tables. Although NeuroStore labels some models as 'fixed effects', the document shows cross-subject, between-subject regression and omnibus group analyses with whole-brain inference, supporting inclusion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, PET, task>baseline only, or only between-group contrasts without within-task contrasts) are met based on the provided record.

This fMRI study tested human participants in an olfactory decision-making task (sniffing odors and making perceptual/pleasantness/intensity decisions), meeting I4. It reports within-task decision contrasts (correct > error) and parametric modulation with discriminability (ΔI) mapping onto perceptual difficulty, meeting I5. The model was fit at the group level over the whole brain (group random-effects, one-sample t-test) and peak coordinates are reported, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults, satisfying I7. Although inference used small-volume corrections (ROI-restricted SVC), the analyses were estimated over the whole brain and group-level voxelwise maps and reported coordinates, so this does not invoke E6 (only-ROI reports). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task (cups task) in healthy human participants and includes within-group contrasts directly comparing risky versus sure choices (risky > sure), meeting the review’s risky-DM contrast requirements. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with whole-brain inference and peak-level FWE correction; coordinate peaks are reported. Thus it satisfies whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET modality, ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, comparisons only to baseline, or non-empirical work) are met. The NeuroStore record provides sufficient detail to confirm I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This study reports fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analogue Risk Task) in human participants, including within-subject contrasts comparing risk vs control (active pump > control pump) and decision-related contrasts (cash-out, explosion) analyzed at the group level. Models were fit over the whole brain with voxelwise inference (Alphasim cluster correction) and peaks reported in Table 1. Participants are healthy humans. The contrasts are condition-versus-condition (risk > control), satisfying the review’s risky-DM contrast definitions. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline-only, not connectivity-only). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task fMRI data collected during the Wheel of Fortune task, a risky decision-making paradigm, with participants making monetary choices under varying probabilities. It includes decision-versus-control contrasts (Money > Control) and condition contrasts (abstinent vs satiated) and interaction contrasts relevant to risk processing. Analyses are group-level paired t-tests fit over the whole brain with cluster-corrected inference and reported peak coordinates (Table t2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Participants are a clinical substance-using group (nicotine dependence), which is acceptable. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no PET, no implicit-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in human participants (n=15) performing an economic decision-making task manipulating reward probability and time, with analyses targeting uncertainty (Shannon entropy). It includes a within-group parametric modulation (BOLD positively correlated with entropy) that maps higher vs lower uncertainty (equivalent to “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”), reported as whole-brain, group-level results (peaks/coordinates). These meet the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making scope. Whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects models are used and results are reported in tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, and reports whole-brain task activation). Therefore the article satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results from a probability discounting task (monetary rewards with explicit probabilities), which qualifies as risky decision-making. It includes a free>forced (decision vs. control) contrast (and a conjunction free>forced across delay and probability tasks), meeting the requirement for an experimental-task > control-task comparison. Analyses are voxelwise whole-brain with FWE-corrected inference and coordinate reporting. Although the study also includes delay discounting (intertemporal choice, typically excluded), the presence of a qualifying risky-DM contrast from the probability task satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria. Participant groups and coordinate reporting are acceptable. No exclusion criteria (PET, ROI-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

This Neuron fMRI study examined financial (risky) decision-making with human participants (n=19) performing a stock/bond choice task, meeting the review scope. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., gain > loss) and parametric modulation by uncertainty, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Model fitting was conducted over the whole brain and at least one analysis (negative correlation with uncertainty) reports whole-brain inference and corrected peaks; coordinates/tables of peaks are provided. Participants are healthy adults and whole-brain results are reported in tables, satisfying I4–I8. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not task>baseline only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the study is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion: The study reports a reversal-learning task and group comparisons of model-derived reward prediction error signals, but does not present a decision-making contrast of the types required (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Specifically, only between-group contrasts (OCD > controls) of RPE parametric effects are reported. Therefore the study is excluded because: (E8) it reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no accompanying within-group unmasked whole-brain task effect, and (E5) the task does not correspond to the review’s target categories (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrast within the task reported).

The Yellow Light Game is a risky decision-making task (I4 met). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (I6 met). Participant sample is acceptable (I7 met). Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/peaks is present (I8 met). However, the NeuroStore extraction only reports contrasts that compare social context during the same decision type (e.g., Go decision: peer > parent; Stop decision: peer > parent) and PPI connectivity differences by context. No contrast of interest for the meta-analysis is provided (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or decision > control) — therefore I5 is NOT met. No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E9) are triggered by the available information (exclusion set=[]). Because the required decision-making contrast (I5) is absent, the study is excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (cups gambling task) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Multiple within-subject contrasts compare decision-making conditions (e.g., Riskwin > Norisk; Norisk > Riskwin; Risk > Norisk), with random-effects group models and reported MNI peak coordinates. Results meet the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting, and participants are an eligible group. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, PET, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI BOLD during a risky decision-making task (risky-gains task) with explicit risky vs safe choices (risky response > safe response), matching the review’s risky-DM contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; peaks reported in tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Both within-group contrasts (younger and older men: risky > safe) and a between-group interaction (older vs younger risky > safe) are present. The task and contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), participants are human and within accepted age ranges, and results are reported as coordinates/tables (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI task where participants made decisions (choose obtain reward vs avoid punishment) about tones varying in ambiguity/valence, directly addressing ambiguous decision-making. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (second-level GLM, parametric contrasts) with cluster-level FWE inference and coordinates/tables provided. Contrasts include parametric and quadratic effects that index ambiguity (strongest response for the most ambiguous tone) and valence comparisons (positive > negative), matching allowed ambiguous-DM contrasts. Participants are human and acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment (n=48 adolescents) that includes the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) and contrasts comparing task conditions (e.g., Pumps > Control; cash-outs parametrically varying with reward). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The paper therefore meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition-vs-condition/task-vs-control contrasts relevant to risk), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used a cued reward-anticipation/receipt task (gains, losses, neutral) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Although group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs are reported (satisfying I6) and participants of a clinical group are included (I7), and whole-brain results are presented in tables (I8), the task does not manipulate uncertainty/risk/ambiguity nor report contrasts of the accepted forms (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study reports an fMRI gambling (risky decision-making) task with healthy human participants and within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (Risk_Disadv > Risk_Adv and sub-conditions). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with inference over the whole brain and coordinate peaks reported, meeting the requirement for whole-brain task activation maps. The contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (meets I4) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with reported peaks (meets I6 and I8). Participants are an acceptable group (healthy adults; meets I7). However, the NeuroStore-extracted contrasts are comparisons of prime types (Novel > Familiar) and cross-subject regressions relating the novel>familiar effect to risk-taking and exploratory traits. The record does not report any qualifying decision-making condition contrast of the form required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty) nor a decision-task > active control-task contrast. Because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (Group by Decision; Group by Outcome) without any unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or simple condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., risky > safe). Exclusion criteria met: E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or task > control within the whole-brain unmasked maps). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study reports task-based fMRI BOLD data acquired while human participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task, a risky decision-making paradigm, satisfying I4. It includes within-group, task-related contrasts that parametrize probability of explosion (ChooseInflate*P(explode), ChooseWin*P(explode)), which represent risk-level comparisons (analogous to high-risk > low-risk or parametric risk effects), satisfying I5. Analyses were modeled and tested voxelwise over the whole brain at the group level (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain), satisfying I6. Participants are human (healthy young adults), so I7 is met. Results are reported with peak coordinates and standard thresholding, consistent with I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition/parametric decision contrasts (not against implicit baseline), the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and within-group task effects are present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports fMRI data collected while participants made monetary choices between risky and safe lotteries (risky decision-making). It includes a within-group parametric contrast correlating activity with increasing probability of reward in the regulator group (a valid risky-DM contrast analogous to high-risk > low-risk or parametric risk effect). Model fitting and statistical inference were conducted voxelwise over the whole brain and group-level peaks/coordinates are reported (Table t2). Participants (n=20) are an acceptable group. Although a seed-based connectivity analysis is also reported, whole-brain task activation results are present, so E7 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task risky contrast/parametric modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables).

The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group contrast (Comparison subjects > patients) from a whole-brain analysis of an Iowa Gambling Task. Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinate table). Exclusion met: E8 — the document shows only between-group contrasts with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task-effect contrast (no risky>safe, task>control, or within-task parametric contrast reported separately). I5 is not met because there is no within-task decision-making condition contrast or task-vs-control contrast presented. Therefore the study must be excluded per E8.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (BART) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (parametric modulation by pump number), so it satisfies I4 (risky DM task) and I6 (whole-brain task-evoked map). Participant sample is acceptable (substance users and controls), satisfying I7. However, the NeuroStore record only reports a between-group interaction contrast (Control > Methamphetamine: modulation by pump number) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task-condition contrasts reported. Because the paper, as represented here, appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criterion I5 (a within-task decision-making condition contrast or task>control contrast) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded for E8.

The study reports an fMRI investigation using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making), meeting the review topic. The NeuroStore record and abstract explicitly describe voxel-level analyses and report whole-brain peak coordinates (Table 3) for Active-choice and Passive no-choice conditions, indicating group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. At least one within-task decision-making contrast/condition (active-choice versus passive/no-choice or risk-related condition contrasts) is reported. Participants are human (twin sample), and coordinate tables/peaks are provided. Although the paper also reports ROI-based genetic-correlation analyses, whole-brain activation peaks are present, so the ROI-only exclusion does not apply. I therefore include the study for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI. If full text shows that the reported peaks are only condition>baseline (implicit baseline) contrasts rather than condition-vs-condition, inclusion could be re-evaluated; but the available record and ‘voxel-level analysis’ language support inclusion.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in which participants performed a decision-making (prediction) task under uncertainty and a control reporting task; contrasts compare prediction > control (e.g., PdY and PdE vs CtY and CtE). These are condition-versus-control-task contrasts relevant to uncertain/ambiguous decision-making. Analyses were estimated and inferred over the whole brain (voxelwise) and report coordinate peaks and corrected statistics. Participants are human healthy adults and results include within-task whole-brain activations (activations common to older and young) as well as age-related effects. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not against implicit baseline (task>control used), results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not PET, and not only between-group with no within-group task effect. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This Neuron fMRI study reports whole-brain BOLD results from a gambling (risky decision-making) task in healthy humans, with multiple within-task contrasts comparing decision types (Lmin, Gmax, Pmax choices; compensatory vs simplifying choices) and a gain>loss outcome contrast. Analyses are group-level, random-effects, voxelwise, with whole-brain inference and cluster correction. Sample sizes (n=20–22) and participant characteristics are reported. These details satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported in standard coordinate space). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not contrasts vs baseline only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports human fMRI data of decision making under uncertainty (probabilistic/ambiguous decisions) with within-task contrasts (Uncertain decisions > Certain decisions) matching the meta-analysis targets. Analyses were performed and reported as whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (model fit and inference over whole brain) with coordinates in tables. Participants were healthy humans. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Although the group analysis used a fixed-effects model, the document nevertheless provides whole-brain group contrast maps suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements and none of the exclusions.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a sequential decision-making (foraging) task with probabilistic outcomes, fitting the review scope of risky decision-making. The paper reports within-group, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts/parametric modulators (e.g., momentary probability of foraging success, choice uncertainty, heuristic vs optimal policy discrepancies) with FWE-corrected inference, satisfying requirements for condition-vs-condition/task contrasts and whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy adults and coordinates/peaks are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts).

The study is excluded because its reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) only: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest', with AlphaSim cluster correction. Therefore it does not provide the required group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps (I6 not met) and meets exclusion E6. Additionally, the extracted contrasts are reported as between-group interactions (HC vs OB) with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effects presented, meeting exclusion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision-making task), I5 (decision-making contrasts, e.g., safe vs risky following a loss), I7 (acceptable participant groups). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete for screening.

Excluded (E8): The NeuroStore record reports only an omnibus between-group contrast identifying risk-related differences between HIV- and HIV+ groups during the Risky Gains task, with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., risky > safe) provided in the record. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in standard coordinate/table form). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear within-task or task-versus-control decision-making contrast is reported in the extracted analyses). Because the study appears to report only between-group contrasts without accompanying whole-brain within-group task effects, it meets exclusion criterion E8 and is therefore excluded.

Exclusion decision because the NeuroStore record does not provide a group-level fMRI whole-brain activation map. Specifically: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (the paper reports a decision-making contrast: unambiguous > high ambiguity), I7 (participant sample acceptable), I8 (results reported in extractable format). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the record does not provide evidence of an fMRI scan contrast or fMRI task activation maps—the reported measures and model are electrophysiological and EEG source-localization), I6 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI task-evoked statistical map is reported in the extracted analyses). Because I4 and I6 are required and are not satisfied in the provided document, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study scanned human participants (n=15) performing a Monetary Incentive Delay / gambling task that manipulated reward value and uncertainty. Reported contrasts include within-task comparisons relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making (e.g., high > low reward value; increasing reward uncertainty; parametric modulations), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise maps (model fit over whole brain; FDR-corrected voxelwise results; reported peak coordinates). Participants are healthy adults. The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for risky/ambiguous decision-making fMRI contrasts and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports fMRI BOLD data collected while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (Random Dot Kinematogram), fulfilling I4. The reported contrasts include a within-group task comparison (dots vs. arrows) and an interaction involving ramp regressors, which constitutes a decision-making condition contrast (perceptual task versus an alternative/control task), satisfying I5. The analyses were fit and inference was performed over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample (n=20, ages reported) meets I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: the study does not rely on implicit baseline contrasts only, is not PET, includes whole-brain results rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses, and reports within-group task contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study does not test a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task contrast required for inclusion. Although the paper reports whole-brain task activations (Reappraise > Maintain) and reports whole-brain connectivity (PPI) for face viewing, these tasks are emotion regulation and passive/valence viewing rather than decision-making contrasts of the types specified (risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy, etc.). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no fMRI of a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as ambiguous>non-ambiguous or perceptual hard>easy). Exclusion applied: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete enough for screening.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task and reports risky>safe contrasts, but all reported analyses are ROI-based and report only between-group interactions with no whole-brain, unmasked group-level task activation maps. Exclusion criteria E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) is met, and E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect) also applies.
