Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (risky > safe contrast reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in extractable format). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked map). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (CUPS) and reports whole-brain, group-level maps; however, all NeuroStore-extracted task results are between-group contrasts (NonMeth > Meth, interactions, and cross-subject regressions) and PPI connectivity. The record contains no unmasked, within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., risky > safe within a group or task > control) or standalone within-group whole-brain task effect. Therefore it meets exclusion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect) despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

The study reports event-related fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) and includes within-group contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., risky > safe; decision-making > control). Multiple group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) one-sample t-test analyses are reported with peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are human healthy adults. Results are not ROI-only, not PET, and are not connectivity-only; contrasts are condition-versus-condition or task-versus-control rather than task>baseline. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (motion/color coherence) with within-group, voxelwise parametric modulation analyses of motion/color coherence (i.e., hard vs easy / low vs high coherence contrasts). Model was fit over the whole brain and results are reported as peak coordinates (Table 1, MNI). Although the group analysis used fixed-effects and the sample is small (n=5), the review’s inclusion criteria accept any participant groups and require whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps, which are present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition parametric effects (not task>baseline only), not PET, not ROI-only, and not connectivity-only. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task and reports ROI-restricted inference despite fitting models over the whole brain. It does not clearly test a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation as defined by the review, nor does it present the required decision-condition contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Crucially, inference was restricted to a region of interest (no unmasked whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), violating the review's whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore it must be excluded.

Study reports task-based fMRI during a gambling (risky decision-making) task and includes one or more condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., High-Risk > Low-Risk). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; voxelwise GLM/ANOVA) with reported peak coordinates. Participants are human and within the acceptable age range. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) satisfying I4. It reports explicit decision-making contrasts (e.g., Mean Risk > Mean Control; Linear Risk > Linear Control) satisfying I5. Analyses were performed and inferred over the whole brain with voxelwise models (FLAME; whole-brain inference) satisfying I6. Participant sample (adolescents, including substance users) is acceptable per I7. Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables, which meets I8. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky DM (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the paper provides task activation maps rather than only connectivity or only between-group contrasts. Therefore the article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task with intravenous alcohol vs placebo. It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky vs safe choices and feedback conditions (e.g., Risky > Safe, Win > Loss), reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain, Talairach coordinates, cluster correction reported), and results are reported as peak coordinates (Table t1). Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI: I4 (fMRI risky task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts such as Risky > Safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing an ambiguity decision-making task (contrast UNC: Uncertain > Certain), fulfilling ambiguous-DM contrast definitions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (1-sample t-test; model fit and inference over whole brain; peaks in Table 1), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are human healthy adults. Results are reported as coordinate peaks. Although the abstract describes seed-based connectivity, the paper also provides unmasked whole-brain task activation maps/peaks, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only (E6, E7) do not apply. No contrasts are against implicit baseline/rest. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study used fMRI with a risky decision-making task (BART) and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts and coordinates; however, the NeuroStore record indicates only between-group contrasts and group-by-condition interactions (and a seed-based connectivity result). There is no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrast comparing decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe or equivalent within-group parametric contrasts) reported in the document. This meets exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without accompanying whole-brain within-group task effects). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task decision-making contrast like risky>safe reported). Therefore excluded under E8.

Exclusion E8 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts (SI+ vs SI− parametric modulator and a group-difference peak) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task—Balloon Analog Risk Task), I5 (a decision-making-related contrast is reported, albeit as a between-group contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: none additionally, but exclusion E8 overrides inclusion because only between-group contrasts are reported and no within-group whole-brain task effect is available in the record.

Exclusion IDs met: E6 (only ROI analyses reported; model fit and inference restricted to bilateral nucleus accumbens ROI) and E5 (task is a music-reward learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy human volunteers). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task — NOT met; the task involves learning cue–music associations and reward prediction errors for musical consonance/dissonance), I5 (no eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast of the specified forms; reported contrasts are RPE-related or consonant > dissonant), I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps reported; analyses and inference are ROI-restricted). Because the study fails required inclusion criteria I4, I5, and I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (and E5), it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) experiment in healthy humans performing a perceptual/target-detection task with graded similarity and ambiguity manipulations. It includes within-group contrasts/parametric modulators directly indexing ambiguity and similarity (i.e., decision uncertainty/perceptual difficulty) and a direct contrast (morph distractors > target). Analyses were conducted and reported at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference (FDR voxel-level) and peaks/tables are provided. These facts satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for (i) an fMRI perceptual/ambiguous decision-making task, (ii) at least one relevant decision-making contrast/parametric effect, (iii) whole-brain group-level results, and (iv) reporting of coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The report only presents between-group interaction contrasts (group × choice mode) and modulation differences (HCs > IGD interaction) at the whole-brain level; no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, task > control) are reported. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task - BART), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise inference reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying within-task or task>control decision-making contrast reported). Full text appears complete in the record.

This paper reports fMRI experiments where participants made predictions under parametrically varying uncertainty (experiment 1: probability-based/external uncertainty; experiment 2: rule-knowledge/internal uncertainty). Contrasts include decision-making conditions compared to an active control (e.g., p=1.0... > Control; Trained/Learned... > Control) and parametric modulation of uncertainty. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain GLMs (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants are human healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, includes within-group task contrasts). Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) gambling task that manipulates risk (symmetric, positively skewed, negatively skewed gambles) and examines choices and brain activity during decision-making. The abstract and NeuroStore data describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level regression) and a direct contrast comparing positively versus negatively skewed trials. Results are reported as coordinate peaks (tables) and whole-brain cluster-corrected inference. Participants are human adults (n=32). These elements satisfy all required inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain group maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only, and is empirical).

The study includes an fMRI reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) and reports a reward>punishment contrast, satisfying I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task) and I5 (a within-task decision-making contrast). However, although the GLM was fit over the whole brain, statistical inference was explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest (bilateral ventral striatum) and only ROI results are reported. This means the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map, failing I6 and meeting exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study used task-fMRI during a risky gambling task (meets I4) and reports within-task contrasts (Non/Imp > Low/High) comparing decision conditions (meets I5). Participants are an acceptable group (healthy adults; meets I7). However, the reported analysis is a seed-based task connectivity analysis (gPPI) with inference on connectivity parameters; no unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map is reported. This meets exclusion E7 (studies reporting only seed-based/effective connectivity without whole-brain task activation). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain task-activation map (I6 not met).

The study used fMRI during a risky monetary decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports within- and between-group contrasts comparing risky versus safer selections, so it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky decision-making), I5 (decision-making contrasts: risky > safe), and I7 (acceptable participant groups). However, the NeuroStore record shows all reported statistical analyses were fit and tested within predefined ROIs (OFC/VLPFC and ACC) with small-volume correction; the document does not present or describe any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Based on this, the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (identifying vocal emotions) and includes within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions (unbiased vs biased and related contrasts), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Analyses were fit and inference performed over the whole brain (voxelwise) with thresholding and reported peak coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participants are healthy humans (n=16). Whole-brain results are reported (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the perceptual decision-making meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot kinematogram) and reports within-group contrasts that directly compare decision conditions (e.g., 100% > 0% coherence and 0° > 90° distance from category boundary), which constitute perceptual difficulty/coherence contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and inference was conducted across the whole brain with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants meet allowable groups. Results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied; none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Note: sample size is small (n=9) but the meta-analysis allows any participant group/age, so this does not preclude inclusion.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making (framing/gambling) task and reported condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., sure vs gamble across frames), satisfying I4 and I5. However, the reported group-level activation results are inference-restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (and the other reported results are seed-based PPI connectivity). No unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map or whole-brain inference is reported for the task contrasts. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a decision-making task (selecting between two oxygen-extraction systems) and explicitly models a state-change uncertainty signal (a parametric modulation), which maps onto uncertainty/ambiguity-related decision processes. At least one appropriate contrast is reported (within-group parametric modulation of state-change uncertainty; between-group parametric modulation of expected-value differences and task contrasts), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Analyses were fit and inferences made at the whole-brain, group level with coordinates/peaks reported and cluster-level correction, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Participants are healthy human groups in the eligible age range and results are reported as coordinate peaks in tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and should be included.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: fMRI was conducted while human participants performed a decision-making task manipulating outcome uncertainty (two-choice prediction with 20/50/80% error rates) (I4). The reported contrasts examine task × error-rate effects (uncertainty) and task × group × error-rate interactions, i.e., condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with coordinate tables and cluster correction reported (Model fit over: whole brain; Talairach coordinates; reported peaks) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I6) and coordinate reporting is acceptable (I8). Participant sample is acceptable per review rules (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not only task>rest (E3), not PET (E4), task is decision-making under uncertainty (not an excluded task per E5), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only; E6), and the paper reports within-task uncertainty effects (and a Task × error-rate effect) rather than only between-group contrasts (E8). Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study of a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion discrimination) with within-task contrasts (reliable > neutral; moderate > neutral) that compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with coordinates reported and cluster-level inference, fulfilling whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy adults and results are reported as coordinate tables. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (perceptual DM) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a Wheel of Fortune decision-making task involving risky choices (high vs low probability, risky vs safe selections), meeting the review focus on risky decision-making. It reports within-group contrasts of decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe / low-probability > high-probability) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain for key contrasts) with reported peak coordinates in tables. Participants are human and eligible. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the risky-DM meta-analysis.

The study reports human fMRI data collected during a gambling (risky decision-making) task (card-guessing), with group-level random-effects GLM analyses fit over the whole brain and reported voxelwise peaks in MNI space. It includes an explicit within-group contrast high > low (a riskier>less risky contrast) and multiple parametric modulation contrasts (expected value, variance, expected utility), satisfying condition-versus-condition contrasts. Whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise results are reported (with some ROI small-volume correction for one analysis but other analyses show whole-brain voxelwise thresholds and reported peaks). Thus the paper meets I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task risky contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (participants acceptable), and I8 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI during a gambling (Card-Guessing) task (risky decision-making) and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (reward > neutral, reward > baseline) that match decision-vs-control comparisons. The NeuroStore record lists group-level, whole-brain inference for key contrasts (e.g., reward>neutral, loss>neutral, interaction) with voxelwise FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. Participants are human healthy adults, and results are reported as peak tables (acceptable formats). Although the shared metadata notes ‘model fit over: region of interest’, the record explicitly states whole-brain inference and voxelwise results for several contrasts; on balance the paper provides qualifying whole-brain task activation contrasts for risky decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, non-risk task, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply based on the document provided.

The NeuroStore record indicates an fMRI decision-making task (predict which person will be picked) and whole-brain, voxelwise group results reported in coordinate tables, but the reported contrasts are only between-group (CTL > METH and interactions). The record does not show any unmasked, within-group task contrasts or simple condition-vs-condition decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) or task>active-control that would qualify. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts reported). Included criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-condition contrasts reported).

Excluded because the task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/instrumental conditioning paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or clearly perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses are reported), I7 (participant sample is an eligible human group), I8 (results reported as coordinates/peaks in standard space). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task does not clearly qualify as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM), I5 (there is no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast as defined by the meta-analysis — the reported contrasts reflect learning-type or cue-difficulty in a learning context, e.g., "easy > hard" during probabilistic learning rather than a perceptual difficulty contrast aligned with the meta-analysis definitions). Fulltext_incomplete: false.

The study reports an fMRI task involving perceptual decision-making (odd/even coin-count judgments) with an explicit uncertainty manipulation (Uncertain > Certain), satisfying the decision-making task requirement. Whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise maps are reported (model fit over whole brain; peaks/tables provided), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Contrasts are condition-versus-condition (Uncertain > Certain and related interactions), not task>rest. Participant groups (recovering alcoholics and controls) are acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task contrasts are reported). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) and reports a whole-brain, voxelwise parametric modulation of risk (adjusted pumps) with reported peak coordinates. The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map (voxelwise FWE thresholding) consistent with risky-DM contrasts (parametric high-risk > low-risk). Participants include adolescents with TBI and controls, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only, or only between-group contrasts without within-task effects) are indicated in the provided document. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task (pairs of gambles with probability pie charts) conducted during the decision phase, satisfying I4. The reported analysis examines neural responses to risk (‘‘Neural correlates of family environment in response to risk during the decision phase’’) as a within-group, cross-subject regression—this constitutes a within-task risky decision-making contrast relevant to I5. The model was fit and inference performed over the whole brain with voxelwise group-level GLM and reported peak coordinates (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; Table t1), meeting I6 and I8. Participant sample (adolescents, n=135) is an acceptable group per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Full text appears present in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This event-related fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task in which subjects chose between stimuli with monetarily determined probabilistic rewards and punishments, i.e., decision-making under uncertainty. The paper reports multiple within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level contrasts (e.g., Reward>Control, Reward>Punishment) and parametric modulations of reward/punishment magnitude. Whole-brain group random-effects analyses and reported peak coordinates are present. These facts satisfy inclusion requirements: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with probabilistic outcomes), I5 (within-task contrasts and task>control contrasts present), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/ connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and not non-empirical). Confidence is moderate (0.75) because the task is a learning/reversal paradigm rather than an explicit risk-manipulation like high-risk vs low-risk; however, the probabilistic outcomes and task>control contrasts make it eligible under the review’s allowable forms.

Excluded because the study used a delay-discounting (intertemporal) task, which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (Exclusion E5). NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain, group-level results (I6) and condition contrasts (hard>easy, easy>control) meeting I5, and participant/sample criteria are acceptable (I7) with coordinate-table reporting acceptable (I8). However I4 (task type: risky/ambiguous/perceptual) is not met. Additionally, the extraction appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked within-group task effect maps, so Exclusion E8 also applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5, E8.

The task is a social jumping-to-conclusion paradigm using morphed emotional faces (social/emotion decision-making). The review excludes social decision-making tasks (E5). Although the study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI results (I6) and includes eligible participant groups and acceptable reporting (I7, I8), it does not evaluate a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as defined by the meta-analysis (I4 and I5 are not satisfied). The within-task contrasts are last>previous decision trials and emotion blocks, not standard risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts. Therefore the study is excluded under E5.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (n=14) using a perceptual dot-motion decision-making task manipulating stimulus and response conflict via coherence and congruency. It includes within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., high > low stimulus conflict, incongruent > congruent, high > low irrelevant coherence) that compare decision-making conditions rather than task vs baseline. Analyses were group-level and fitted over the whole brain (voxelwise), with peak coordinates reported. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI perceptual decision-making study, contains relevant condition contrasts, provides whole-brain voxelwise results, and reports results clearly. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply.

Excluded because the task is a memory-based navigation/retrieval task and the NeuroStore record does not report any contrast that matches the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty). Thus it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a decision-like task/memory-based choice), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise searchlight inferences reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results/peaks reported). Not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous or perceptual decision-making contrast as required). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports whole-brain fMRI activation during audiovisual exposure that predicts later perceptual classifications of ambiguous phonemes. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise map reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was acquired during audiovisual exposure blocks, but the perceptual decision-making classifications that define the behavior occurred later in time and appear not to have been performed as an in-scanner decision-making task), and I5 (no contrast comparing two decision-making conditions such as hard>easy or ambiguous>non-ambiguous is reported; the reported analysis is a behaviorally weighted parametric association rather than a within-task condition contrast). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E9) are clearly met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I4 and I5 are not met, the study is excluded.

The study reports fMRI during a risky decision-making Wheel of Fortune task (N=23). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus certain trials (Risk > No-Risk; Prob40/60 vs Prob100), reported as whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with tables of peak coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. The contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task vs implicit baseline). Thus all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI whole-brain activation studies are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI BOLD data acquired during a Risky Decision-Making Task (risky vs safe choices), and it includes at least one condition-versus-condition contrast of decision-making (e.g., risky minus safe). Group-level analyses were fit and inference was performed over the whole brain (voxelwise) with reported peak coordinates/tables and cluster correction, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. A within-group cross-subject regression (Dimensional Neuroimaging Results: Interim Marijuana Use Predicting BOLD for Risky Minus Safe Decisions) provides an unmasked, whole-brain within-task effect. Participants (occasional stimulant users) are an acceptable group. Reporting of peaks/tables is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only implicit-baseline contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not report any decision-making contrasts required by I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a gambling/card-guessing decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for gains>losses), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 — the reported contrasts are outcome/feedback contrasts (gain > loss) and an ROI correlation of BOLD with IQ after losses; there are no contrasts that compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguous > non-ambiguous) or a decision task versus an active control task. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . fulltext_incomplete set to false.

Although the paper used fMRI during a gambling/card-guessing task (satisfying I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate tables (I6, I8), and includes healthy participant samples (I7), the reported contrasts focus on feedback/outcome processing (gains vs losses, correct vs wrong), learning-phase interactions, and between-group learner comparisons. The article does not report any contrast that matches the meta-analysis’ required decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy) nor a task>control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. The study is an fMRI experiment with human participants (n=15) performing a perceptual decision-making (2AFC face/house categorization) task (I4). Multiple within-task contrasts compare decision-making conditions (e.g., HV > FV, cost > neutral, parametric effects of categorical uncertainty, ‘easier perceptual decisions’), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts (I5). Several analyses report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects results with FWE cluster-level thresholding and reported peaks/tables (I6, I8). Participant group is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion criteria met: E6. The report shows fMRI of a risky decision task (Wheel of Fortune) with the qualifying contrast high-risk (25%) > low-risk (75%) (within-group). Participants are adolescents with depressive disorder (allowed). However, all reported analyses were ROI-based: model fit and inference restricted to ROI with small-volume correction (voxel-level, p<0.05) across ACC, OFC, mPFC; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported. Therefore the study does not satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6) and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task risky contrast high-risk > low-risk), I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (judging average color/shape of arrays) with parametric within-task contrasts indexing uncertainty of mean (UMr/UMi) and evidence variability (UVr/UVi). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; group t-tests; reported peak tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants (n=20, healthy adults) are acceptable. The contrasts are condition-vs-condition parametric modulations of perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (analogous to hard>easy or high uncertainty>low uncertainty). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8.

The study reports a group-level fMRI whole-brain voxelwise analysis of a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with a contrast comparing high risk/reward > moderate risk/reward. The model was fit over the whole brain with inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are human adolescents performing an explicit risky decision task. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI during risky decision-making (I4), a condition-vs-condition risky contrast (I5), whole-brain group-level results (I6), acceptable participant group (I7), and that whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Detailed reporting (model, task, sample, thresholding) supports inclusion.

The study reports a task-based fMRI whole-brain group analysis of risky decision-making using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART). The reported contrast is a within-group parametric modulation of risk level (Pumps parametric), which constitutes a decision-condition contrast indexing risk level. The model was fit and inference performed at the whole-brain group level (one-sample t-test) with reported peak coordinates. Participants are human smokers (acceptable sample). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. The NeuroStore record serves as the article representation, and the full-text is available via this record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a risky (gambling) decision-making task (Card-Guessing gambling task). It includes multiple within-group contrasts and parametric modulations comparing decision conditions (preferential vs judgment-based choices; intradimensional differences in probability and payoff; unidimensional CPT utilities), satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts. Several analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps (second-level one-sample and paired t-tests with whole-brain inference listed for multiple analyses), and coordinates/peaks are reported. Participants are healthy humans. Reporting includes whole-brain tables/peaks, meeting acceptable report formats. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study uses a reversal-learning task (probabilistic feedback) and reports whole-brain group maps and an EEG-informed within-group parametric modulation, but it does not report any qualifying decision-making condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy) or a decision-task > active control contrast. Reported analyses are between-group contrasts (Controls > ADHD; ADHD > Controls) of parametric modulators (RPEoutcome, RPEcue) and a within-group FRN regressor—these are parametric/association maps rather than condition-versus-condition or task-versus-control contrasts required by I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level results), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-vs-decision or task-vs-control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) directly apply based on the provided document.

The study reports an fMRI experiment (n=17) using a perceptual judgment task (color similarity and preference) with within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions (ISD vs EVD, ISD vs ESD, ESD vs EVD). Model fitting was done at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and results are reported as thresholded peaks (FDR-corrected voxelwise), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The task includes a perceptual/veridical decision condition (external veridical decision) and contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not against implicit baseline). Thus it meets the fMRI, decision-making contrast, whole-brain, participant eligibility, and reporting criteria for inclusion in a meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI study of risky decision-making with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FWE voxel-level) and coordinate peaks reported. However, the reported contrasts are omnibus/between-group (Group × Valence interaction; Main Effect of Feedback listed as omnibus, between-group) and no unmasked, whole-brain within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe, risk > certainty) or task > control are provided. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying whole-brain within-group task effect) and fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5. It does satisfy I4, I6, I7, and I8. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study uses fMRI during a perceptual decision-making (2AFC) task and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (peaks/tables), but it does not present any of the required decision-making condition contrasts (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, or perceptual task > control). Instead, reported contrasts are parametric model-based correlations (e.g., reward prediction error, V(t), model comparisons WITH vs WITHOUT stimulus-discriminability). These model-based associations do not match the inclusion criterion I5 which requires a direct decision-making condition comparison or task-versus-control contrast. Therefore the study fails I5 despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

The study reports fMRI (BOLD) during the Balloon Analog Risk Task, a canonical risky decision-making task, satisfying I4. It provides multiple condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Pumps > Control, PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, group and within-group contrasts) meeting I5. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain maps with inference reported over the whole brain (FWE cluster correction; MNI coordinates and peak tables), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups include smokers and nonsmokers (eligible per I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and within-group task effects are present (so E3,E4,E5,E6,E7,E8,E9 do not apply). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a risky decision-making task (Social Analogue Risk Task), meeting I4. It provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM; model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates, meeting I6 and I8. The reported contrasts include within-task parametric modulation and regression relating brain activity during decision events (cash-out PM) to social sensitivity (a between-subject regressor), which constitutes an acceptable within-task decision-making contrast for risky decisions (meets I5). Participant ages (12–16) and healthy sample meet I7. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not PET, not connectivity-only, and contrasts are not only task>implicit baseline. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed a gambling (risky decision-making) task and includes multiple within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., Positive EV > Negative EV). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise, with coordinates/peaks reported. Participants are healthy. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a risky decision-making task (participants decide whether to take gambles), satisfying I4. It contains within-subject contrasts comparing decision conditions (Riskloss > Riskwin and Riskwin > Riskloss), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; group random-effects OLS; voxelwise correlations and whole-brain inference), satisfying I6. Participants are human healthy adults (n=14), which is acceptable per I7. Whole-brain results are reported (peaks, inference, thresholds), consistent with I8. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), it is fMRI (not PET), task is risky DM (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the study is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an event-related fMRI study in humans (Iowa Gambling Task) with a within-group contrast comparing risky > safe decisions, satisfying the risky decision-making contrast form. A group-level, whole-brain random-effects analysis was performed (model fit over whole brain; second-level one-sample t-test reported) with voxel-level correction (p, corrected < 0.05) and reported peak coordinates. Participants are healthy humans (n=14). Results are reported in tables/peaks. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only ROI; not only connectivity; not task>baseline only). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study used fMRI during a card-guessing (gambling) task (risky decision-making) and reports condition-versus-condition contrasts. It includes within-group contrasts (e.g., experimental > control for controls) and between-condition contrasts (high vs low probability/magnitude), satisfying the requirement for decision-condition comparisons. All reported analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise models with corrected cluster inference and coordinates reported. Participant groups (healthy and substance users) are acceptable. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and within-group whole-brain effects are present so E8 is not triggered).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the perceptual decision-making meta-analysis. It used fMRI BOLD while human subjects performed a perceptual decision task (random-dot motion coherence) (I4). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision difficulty/coherence (high > low and low > high coherence), and the low-coherence > high-coherence contrast directly matches the accepted perceptual-DM form ("low coherence > high coherence") (I5). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps using a mixed-effects model and report peak coordinates (I6, I8). Participant sample (n=8, adults) is acceptable per participant inclusion (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition not baseline (not E3), modality is fMRI not PET (not E4), task is perceptual DM (not E5), whole-brain results are reported (not E6), and this is an empirical task activation study (not E7/E8/E9).

The study used fMRI in human participants performing an ambiguous categorization decision task (inverse base rate effect) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps. The reported contrasts are within-group parametric modulators (Similarity > 0, Similarity < 0, Dissimilarity > 0) reflecting trial-by-trial decision-related signals, which qualify as within-task decision-making contrasts related to ambiguity. Analyses were fit over the whole brain with cluster-corrected inference and peak coordinates reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual categorization task (speech vs. non-speech blends) and so meets I4; participant eligibility is acceptable (I7), and results are reported in standard formats (I8). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any qualifying decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, low-coherence>high-coherence) — instead reported contrasts are between-group (Good>Poor, Poor>Good), Time (1st>2nd), and Feedback. Decision-related contrasts are reported with inference restricted to ROIs (no whole-brain task contrast reported), and the only whole-brain contrast available addresses feedback processing (omnibus, between-group) rather than a within-task decision-making effect. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast) and I6 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked decision contrast). It also meets exclusion criteria E6 (decision contrasts reported only with ROI inference/no whole-brain results) and E8 (only between-group contrasts reported with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, but the reported analyses are age-group (developmental) effects and correlations with parametric valuation regressors rather than contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe) or a task > control. NeuroStore shows only between-group/age effects (no unmasked within-group task contrast or decision-condition contrast), so it meets exclusion E8 (only between-group contrasts reported). Included criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion I5 (a decision-condition contrast as specified) is not met. Full text appears available for screening.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task — it is a probabilistic reversal reward-learning task focused on reward prediction errors/valence and surprise). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables/peaks). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrast of the admitted forms for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM — analyses are parametric RPE/modulator associations rather than condition contrasts like risky>safe or hard>easy). The fMRI data are whole-brain and group-level, but the decision-making domain and contrast types required by the meta-analysis are not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI meta-analysis: it used fMRI with the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky DM) (I4); it reports within-task contrasts comparing decision vs directed/control conditions (e.g., DecBa > DirBa and decision win/loss contrasts) satisfying the required contrast forms (I5); group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and inference are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain, peaks/tables provided) fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I8); participant groups (adolescents with conduct/substance disorders and controls) are within acceptable scope (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and includes within-group effects).

The study reports fMRI during a risky decision-making task (driving simulation) with adolescents and provides within-group condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Go > Stop and Stop > Go, decisions following crash vs no-crash) that map directly onto risky vs safe decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (group-level single-sample t-tests; model fit and inference over whole brain; coordinates/peaks reported; cluster correction described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline-only, includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion applied: E6 (study reports only ROI-based analyses with inference restricted to 116 ROIs; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant groups of acceptable ages/conditions). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task not clearly one of the review’s target decision-making tasks as framed for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM contrasts in the required forms), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy — contrasts are reward outcome valence: rewarded correct > punished correct), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-activation map; analyses are ROI-restricted). Because E6 is met (ROI-only reporting), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (2AFC) task (I4). It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (NEGATIVE > NEUTRAL-N and POSITIVE > NEUTRAL-P) satisfying the requirement for a condition-vs-condition contrast (I5). Several analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with inference over the whole brain (Analyses 23428623_analysis_3, _5, _6), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participant sample is healthy adults (allowed by I7). Whole-brain results are reported with peak tables (Analyses report peak tables), acceptable per I8. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not against implicit baseline (E3), modality is fMRI (not PET, E4), the task is perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are present (not ROI-only, E6), and the study is empirical (not E9). Therefore all necessary inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The NeuroStore record reports a whole-brain fMRI study of a gambling/uncertainty decision-making task with a voxelwise uncertain > certain contrast, but the only reported analysis is a between-group interaction (stimulant users vs controls for uncertain>certain). This meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, but the study document appears to report ONLY a between-group contrast/interaction with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation maps. That triggers exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts reported). Full text is available in the record (not incomplete).

This study reports an fMRI experiment of decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous/risky) in humans (n=64). It includes within-group contrasts of decision-making versus an active control (decision/event > counting; information gathering > counting), satisfying the requirement for task-versus-control contrasts. Model fitting and inference were performed whole-brain at the group level (voxelwise; FWE-corrected peaks reported), and coordinate tables are provided. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not versus implicit baseline/rest, the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and results are task-evoked within-group effects (not only between-group). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports whole-brain, group-level analyses, but the NeuroStore extraction shows only omnibus between-group and time effects (main effects of group/time). No within-task condition contrasts reflecting decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I7 (participants acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no decision-condition vs decision-condition or task>control contrasts reported). Exclusion criterion met: E8 (only between-group/time contrasts reported with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous DM) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses, but the reported analyses are omnibus between-group contrasts (group and group×condition interaction) and reported peaks. No unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or task>control contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous or decision > baseline) are reported in this document. Therefore the study reports only between-group contrasts and meets exclusion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during ambiguous decision-making), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise model fit), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying within-task or task>control contrast reported in the extracted analyses). Full text appears complete for screening.

Excluded under E5: the task is an instrumental probabilistic reward-learning paradigm (reward prediction errors and emotional modulation) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. The paper does not report any qualifying contrasts such as 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguous', or 'hard > easy'. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (eligible participant sample: healthy adults), I8 (results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task per the meta-analysis definitions), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete for screening.

The study reports an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (gender/emotion decisions on facial stimuli) performed by human participants (n=23) and includes appropriate decision-versus-control contrasts (Gender > Control, Emotion > Control, Emotion>Gender, Gender>Emotion). Several group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Model fit over and inference over whole brain for Emotion>Control, Gender>Control, Emotion>Gender, Gender>Emotion), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not only ROI, not only connectivity, contrasts are task vs control rather than implicit baseline).

This study reports an fMRI task involving uncertain reward (participants told reward probabilities were random) and a contrast comparing two task conditions (R anticipation > NI anticipation), which corresponds to an experimental (uncertain/ambiguous reward) task versus a control/no-incentive condition. The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level one-sample t-test with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates. Participant groups are acceptable per review criteria. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task—uncertain reward), I5 (contrast comparing decision-making conditions: experimental task > control task), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise map), I7 (allowed participant groups), and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, PET, baseline-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Note: although the task emphasizes anticipation rather than an explicit active choice on each trial, the record labels the task as reward/value choice and explicitly manipulates uncertainty; given the meta-analysis allowance for experimental task > control task contrasts for risky/ambiguous DM, this study is included.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a wheel-of-fortune choice task (risky decision-making) with probabilistic outcomes, satisfying I4. It reports within-task contrasts (anticipation/omission contrasts across reward magnitude levels) that are condition-versus-condition comparisons within the decision task, satisfying I5. Results are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults (I7). The paper also reports PPI connectivity but crucially includes whole-brain task activation contrasts, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (double-or-quits gambles) and provides within-subject contrasts that compare risky (Play) versus safe (Pass) choices and gain versus loss contexts. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM analyses are reported with FWE-corrected inference and MNI coordinates/peaks. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts such as Play>Pass representing risky>safe), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply. The evidence in the NeuroStore record appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is excluded because the task is an instrumental conditioning (reinforcement learning) paradigm reporting parametric reward- and punishment-prediction error contrasts, without any manipulation or contrast that matches risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making definitions required by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined), I5 (no qualifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text is sufficiently represented in the provided document (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making (mixed gambles) task in human participants (adolescents and adults). It includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Accepted > Rejected, Rejected > Accepted) and cross-subject regressions, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Multiple analyses explicitly state model fit and inference were performed voxelwise over the whole brain with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates, providing group-level whole-brain statistical maps. Participant groups (healthy adolescents and adults) fall within the acceptable age range. Results are reported in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and does not present only baseline contrasts or only between-group contrasts without within-group maps. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

This fMRI study investigates risky decision-making with parametric contrasts for probability, magnitude, expected value, and variance in human participants (meets I4 and I5). However, all reported analyses were fit over predefined regions of interest (striatum and prefrontal cortex) rather than performed/reporting unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps). Included criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts such as variance > expected value), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (reporting of coordinate peaks/tables). Not met: I6 (whole-brain evidence).

This fMRI study scanned human participants performing a reinforcement-learning reward task that manipulated uncertainty about option values and modeled trial-by-trial relative uncertainty. It reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) parametric contrasts of relative uncertainty (within-group) and contrasts of explore>nonexplore, with FWE cluster-level inference and reported peaks. These contrasts correspond to decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous/high- vs low-uncertainty style comparisons) and are not task>rest baselines. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making with uncertainty), I5 (within-task parametric contrast analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty and between-condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI gambling/card-guessing task that manipulates uncertainty (100% vs 50% certainty) during decision-making, meeting the review objective. The reported contrast is a within-task, condition-vs-condition comparison (100% certainty > 50% certainty), which qualifies under I5 (ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects map with whole-brain inference and reported coordinate peaks, satisfying I6 and I8. The imaging modality is fMRI (I4) and participant sample (healthy/adult) is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not task>baseline only (E3), not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7), and not non-empirical (E9). Therefore the study should be included.

The paper reports fMRI BOLD data collected while human participants performed multiple perceptual decision-making tasks (face/house discrimination, emotion discrimination, audiovisual synchrony, and random-dot motion) with task difficulty/ambiguity manipulated. Relevant within-task contrasts compare harder/ambiguous > easier/clear conditions (e.g., noisy > clear faces/houses; noisy > clear happy/angry faces; low-coherence [12%+20%] > 100% motion), matching the perceptual-DM contrast forms (hard > easy/low coherence > high coherence). All reported analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise one-sample tests with FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Participant samples are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not only connectivity). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

EXCLUDED because the reported analyses consist only of a between-group interaction contrast (CN loseshift > SZ winstay) with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect reported. This meets exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning decision-making task), I5 (contrast compares two decision-making trial types: loseshift vs winstay), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise model and inference), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported/coordinates provided). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Consequently the study is excluded under E8.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs. house discrimination) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., hard > easy) and model-based parametric contrasts. Several analyses report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) results with reported peak coordinates (e.g., Accumulation, Face/House drift-rate, Face>House, House>Face, DR>RT), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are healthy human adults (n=18). Results are reported as coordinates/tables. The study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and includes within-group task contrasts rather than baseline-only or between-group-only contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports only region-of-interest analyses (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs, SVC FDR peak-level), so no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing decision tasks), I5 (within-task decision contrasts: decision > rating and easy vs difficult decision contrasts), I7 (healthy participant sample), I8 (results/peaks reported). Not met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps). Therefore the study is excluded for E6.

This fMRI study uses a gambling (risky decision-making) task and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and tables (satisfying I4, I6, I7, and I8). However, all reported contrasts focus on feedback valence (positive > negative) and language modulation (English vs Chinese) or ROI-restricted connectivity, and no contrast compares decision-making conditions of interest (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty) nor a decision task versus an active control. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met.

The study reports fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), includes within-task condition contrasts (Bad Deck > Good Deck) that compare decision-making conditions, and provides group-level whole-brain task activation maps (within-group whole-brain contrasts reported with peak tables). Participants are human and acceptable. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and provides whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group whole-brain contrasts (so E3, E4, E6, E7, E8 do not apply).

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reward (multi-armed bandit) decision-making task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results, but it does not provide any of the required condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy) or a decision-task versus active control-task contrast. The NeuroStore extraction lists only parametric modulation effects (expected value at choice; RPE at outcome) and associated whole-brain maps; these are not among the specific contrast forms required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (coordinate/whole-brain results acceptable). No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I5 is not met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making), and reports condition contrasts (e.g., cash > inflation parametric modulator) relevant to risky decision-making. The NeuroStore record lists multiple reported whole-brain peaks (Tables 3 and 4) and a GLM fit over the whole brain; although one interaction analysis used ROI-restricted inference (FWE SVC), other contrasts have whole-brain coordinate tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy males and acceptable per criteria. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI and provides whole-brain coordinate results suitable for meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met.

The task involves a decision with probabilistic detection (50% chance) where dishonest choices yield larger rewards but risk being caught, which constitutes risky decision-making. fMRI was acquired during outcome presentation and contrasts compare decision conditions (Dis > Hon, Hon > Dis, interaction), satisfying a condition-vs-condition contrast analogous to risky > safe. The analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (model fit and inference over whole brain; reported MNI coordinates and peaks), and results are reported in tables. Participants are human healthy adults. Reporting meets acceptable formats. Therefore I4 (fMRI during risky/decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrast comparing decision conditions), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (participants acceptable), and I8 (results reported clearly) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task (I4). It includes within-task contrasts that directly compare risk levels (high-risk > low-risk) and feedback valence (negative > positive), matching the admissible risky-DM contrasts (I5). The reported analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps (model fit over: whole brain; coordinates reported in tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6, I8). Participant groups are healthy children and adults within acceptable ages, so participant eligibility is met (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not baseline; E3 not met), modality is fMRI (E4 not met), task is a risky DM task (E5 not met), whole-brain results are reported (E6 not met), and this is empirical task activation (E7, E9 not met). Hence the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise condition contrasts (decision vs directed), so inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts and interactions (e.g., All Males > All Females; All Cmp > All Pts) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (e.g., decision > directed) reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts with no accompanying within-group task effect). Based on E8, the study is excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making task and includes the key within-task contrast 'risky response > safe response' (analyses 0–2) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise inference (FDR-corrected or unthresholded contrasts reported) consistent with risky-DM contrasts. Within-group one-sample t-tests are reported for each participant group (normal weight, overweight, obese), and between-group contrasts and ANOVA are also given. The document therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (risky > safe contrast present), I6 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only against implicit baseline (E3), not PET (E4), the task is risky DM (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (not E6), not connectivity-only (not E7), and within-group whole-brain effects are present (so E8 does not apply). Full text appears complete as a derived record. Inclusion is therefore appropriate.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in human participants performing a decision task with explicit risk (wait for a higher offer with risk of losing everything), meeting the review’s task domain for risky decision-making. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Analysis 0: whole-brain cluster-level; additional whole-brain contrasts for choice conflict) and reports peaks/coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The reported contrasts include within-task parametric modulators (precision, expected precision, choice conflict) which represent within-task comparisons of high vs low certainty/uncertainty and thus correspond to admissible within-task contrasts (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Participants are an eligible human sample. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not baseline-only, not PET, not ROI-only, and not connectivity-only. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion: E7 applies — the paper reports only region-restricted (ROI) task analyses and seed-based connectivity (PPI) results without presenting an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked activation map for a decision-making contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision-making task performed during scanning), I5 (decision-making contrast present: risky > safe), I7 (participant group acceptable; adolescents within included age range). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group activation map for a decision-making contrast is reported in the document). Because I6 is not satisfied and E7 is met, the study must be excluded from the task-activation meta-analysis.

The study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision task) and I5 (within-task contrast: Face vs House decision), and I7/I8 (eligible participant group and acceptable reporting). However, all reported group-level results in the document are seed-based effective connectivity (PPI) maps; no unmasked, whole-brain task-activation (task-evoked GLM) contrast map is reported. This violates exclusion criterion E7 (studies reporting only seed-based/effective connectivity without whole-brain task activation). Therefore the study must be excluded. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E7. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I7, I8. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported).

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peaks table) and participant details. However, the reported analysis is a cross-subject regression of activation before risky responses with externalizing score, and the record does not report a condition-vs-condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe or high-risk > low-risk) or a task > active control contrast. Thus it does not provide an eligible decision-making contrast; the only reported effect appears to be activation for risky responses (not contrasted) which effectively makes it a condition-versus-baseline type result. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3.

The study reports an fMRI experiment where human participants performed a perceptual 2AFC decision task (piano vs chair) with parametric variation of stimulus quality (high/medium/low noise). It provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects) testing positive and negative parametric modulations by stimulus quality and response-time parametric effects, thresholded with FWE and reported peak coordinates. These contrasts correspond to perceptual-DM comparisons across difficulty/quality levels (e.g., low vs high quality), satisfying the review’s perceptual decision-making contrast requirement. Participants are within the eligible age/health criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or between-group-only contrasts) apply.

The study used fMRI while human participants made decisions about whether electric circuits were correct and reported certainty/uncertainty. It includes within-group contrasts that directly test uncertainty vs certainty (e.g., Uncertainty > Certainty, Legitimate certainty > Over-estimation), matching the ambiguous-decision contrasts in I5. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with reported peak coordinates (meets I6 and I8). The task is a decision-making task involving uncertainty (meets I4). Participants are healthy humans (consistent with I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not PET, not resting-state, not contrasts vs implicit baseline).
