Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E8 applies: the paper reports a whole-brain group-level analysis only as a between-group interaction (analysis_6: whole-brain reversal of encoding of losses in MDD vs HC). Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI during a risky gambling decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast comparing gains vs losses as a decision-making contrast), I7 (eligible participant groups: MDD patients and healthy controls), I8 (results reported with coordinates/peaks). Inclusion not met: I6 (no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task-evoked group map is reported; the whole-brain result is an interaction/between-group contrast while within-group effects are ROI-restricted). Therefore the study must be excluded under E8.

The study used fMRI while participants performed risky lotteries (and coordination games), reporting whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (e.g., entry games > lotteries; contrasts and correlations involving lotteries and games) with voxelwise inference (FWE cluster-level, p<0.001) and peak coordinates. Participants (n=18) are within eligible groups. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI with risky decision task present), I5 (task-vs-task contrasts / decision-making condition comparisons reported), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task contrasts rather than only baseline contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a decision-making Multi-Armed Bandit task (I4). It reports a within-group parametric modulation of a novelty bonus related to choice (a within-task decision-making contrast), so it meets I5. Participant sample is human and acceptable (I7). However, the reported analysis was fit and tested only within a region-of-interest with a spherical small-volume correction (ventral striatum and midbrain), not as a group-level whole-brain voxelwise map. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI results reported with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study used an fMRI valuation/anticipation task with rewards and punishments but does not manipulate or compare levels of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. No contrasts of the form required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, or hard > easy) are reported — instead the contrasts are parametric modulations of value and saliency and multivariate category/value/saliency effects. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). The paper does report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfying I6) and uses an eligible participant sample (I7); whole-brain results are reported in tables (I8).

Decision: EXCLUDED. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning task investigating reversal and feedback processing, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 — a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map is reported (model fit and inference over whole brain for Analysis 0; peaks reported, MNI space); I7 — participant sample is an acceptable group (healthy adults); I8 — whole-brain results are reported as peaks/coordinates. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — the task is not categorized as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making per the review definitions; I5 — contrasts do not compare decision-making conditions of interest (no risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy); contrasts are error vs correct (final reversal errors > correct responses). Because I4 and I5 are not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (choosing between two lotteries manipulating EV and risk). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., riskier > surer, gain > loss, loss > gain) and parametric modulators of risk and EV. Multiple analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (with tables of peaks and whole-brain inference for several contrasts), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy humans and reported coordinates/tables are available. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study used fMRI during a card-gambling task targeting risky decision-making and reward processing (I4). It reports condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; linear increase with risk; choice/outcome contrasts), satisfying the allowed risky-DM contrast forms (I5). Several analyses report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps with reported peaks and whole-brain inference (Analyses 2, 4, 5), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6); ROI analyses are present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are also reported. Participants are healthy males (acceptable per I7). Whole-brain results are presented as reported peaks/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not PET (E4), not limited to ROI-only results (E6), not resting-state/connectivity-only (E7), not contrasts vs implicit baseline only (E3), and not non-empirical (E9). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusions and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts (e.g., DSU > PSU; omnibus between-group) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-task contrasts or task-versus-control contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, hard>easy). This meets exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task - reward/value choice rock-paper-scissors), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported with whole-brain inference), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task decision-making condition contrast or task>control contrast reported). Full text is complete in the record. Therefore study is excluded under E8.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI risky decision-making task with whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (FWE cluster correction) and contrasts that compare decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe). Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. However, the only reported whole-brain results in the record are labeled as interactions/between-group contrasts (both analyses note “[interaction, between-group]”), and there are no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effects reported. Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies reporting ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect), this study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I4–I8 were satisfied), but E8 applies because only between-group/interaction maps are reported in the provided document.

Exclusion met: E6 — all reported task activation analyses are ROI-restricted (model fit and inference restricted to hippocampus and ROI-based PPI), and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps are reported. Inclusion met: I7 — participant groups (adolescents/adults) are acceptable. Inclusion not met: I4 (the report does not clearly present a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as required by the review—while the task is a probabilistic reinforcement learning paradigm, it is not characterized as a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM contrast in the extracted analyses), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy are reported), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it used fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making (framing) task (I4), reports a within-task decision-making contrast (framing interaction comparing choices under gain vs loss frames) that constitutes a condition-vs-condition decision contrast (I5), and the statistical model was fit over the whole brain at the group level (voxelwise) with reported peak coordinates (satisfying I6 and I8). Participant sample is acceptable (healthy young adults) so I7 is met. Although inference was restricted via small-volume correction (ROI) for thresholding, the model was estimated over the whole brain and coordinates were reported, so this does not trigger exclusion for ROI-only results. The paper also includes PPI analyses, but it additionally reports a task activation contrast, so exclusion criteria E6/E7 are not met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) with within-task contrasts comparing decisions following negative vs positive feedback (e.g., Pumps After Negative Feedback > Pumps After Positive Feedback). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLMs with voxelwise inference and cluster-level FWE correction; results reported as peak coordinates in tables. Participants are human adolescents (age range within eligible bounds). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only, and includes within-group whole-brain task contrasts). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (2AFC face detection) task (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with coordinates/tables of peaks (meets I6 and I8). The authors explicitly test BOLD correlations with reaction time as a measure of task difficulty (a within-task difficulty effect equivalent to the accepted perceptual-DM contrasts such as hard>easy), so it provides at least one decision-related contrast (meets I5). Participants are healthy humans within allowable groups (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical fMRI task data (E3- E9 not met). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

Excluded because the fMRI task does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). The reported fMRI analyses involve source memory and reward reactivation/anticipation, not contrasts such as risky>safe or high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported — e.g., learning-phase whole-brain univariate results), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no decision-making contrasts comparing risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty conditions). Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a gambling (risky decision-making) task and reports whole-brain, coordinate-based results, but the NeuroStore extraction lists only between-group contrasts and interactions (Group, Medication, Group×Valence, Medication×Valence) and does not report any within-group contrast comparing decision conditions (e.g., Gamble > Sure or Risky > Safe). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (coordinates reported in a table). It does NOT meet I5 because no decision-condition-vs-decision-condition contrast (risky > safe, gamble > sure, etc.) is reported. This triggers exclusion criterion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports fMRI (BOLD) data collected while human participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making). The reported analysis is a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) mixed-effects GLM of the parametric modulation of activation to levels of risk, with inference over the whole brain and peaks reported. This satisfies inclusion criteria: I4 (task-based fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task parametric contrast indexing risk levels analogous to high-risk > low-risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical map), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported as peaks). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrast, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening.

The task is a probabilistic reversal-learning (reward-based learning) but the reported contrasts are feedback-valence comparisons (negative > positive, positive > negative) rather than contrasts of risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or hard vs easy as required by I5. Whole-brain group- and within-group maps are reported (I6 satisfied). Participant groups are acceptable (I7 satisfied). Results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables (I8 satisfied). However the study’s task/contrasts do not constitute risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts per the review inclusion rules, so it meets exclusion E5 (task not of interest). Therefore exclude.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with manipulated error rates representing reward (20%), uncertainty (50%), and punishment (80%), satisfying the review’s decision-making domain. It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., 50% > 20%, 80% > 20%, breathing load > anticipation), reported as whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses with coordinates in tables and cluster correction, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participant groups are acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than solely task>baseline, and within-task contrasts are reported). Consequently, all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI experiment involving a perceptual decision-making task (face-house categorization) with within-task contrasts (face > house, house > face) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results (model fit and inference over whole brain, FWE threshold). These satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for perceptual decision-making. The task, contrasts, imaging modality, and whole-brain coordinate reporting meet inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not only task>rest (there are condition-vs-condition contrasts), the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and although effective connectivity (DCM) is discussed, the paper also reports whole-brain activation maps. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI during an ambiguous perceptual categorization task (Mooney images) where participants made categorical decisions (faces, guitars, scrambled). The abstract and extracted analyses describe contrasts comparing object-perception states versus no categorical perception (e.g., Faces/guitars vs inverted faces/scrambled), and the model includes within-group contrasts (parametric modulations and HF vs LF contrasts) tied to task conditions. The GLM was estimated and tested at the whole-brain, group level (voxelwise inference) with coordinates reported (Table 1). Participants are human healthy adults. Thus the paper meets the meta-analysis requirement for a perceptual decision-making fMRI task, contains at least one condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast, reports whole-brain group results, and provides coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, PET, baseline-only contrasts) are violated. Full text is available via the NeuroStore extraction provided.

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group condition contrasts (e.g., 'Win > Lose [contrast, between-group]' and an omnibus between-group F for Lose > Win) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a gambling/risky decision-making task), I5 (condition versus condition contrasts: Win vs Lose), I6 (model fit over whole brain; voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported as peaks/tables). Exclusion criterion met: E8 (the document shows only between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying within-group task effect). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI investigation of gambling (risky decision-making) in healthy human participants. It reports multiple within-group contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., active-choice > no-choice; probability-of-winning parametric modulations; bet-size and expected-value effects) and task-related interactions. Several analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit and inference over whole brain; reported peaks/tables), and coordinates/peak tables are provided. Participants are healthy adults. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (decision-making contrasts comparing conditions and parametric risk effects), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported in tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not only ROI, not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears available from the NeuroStore record.

The Probabilistic Selection Task is a reinforcement-learning paradigm with model-based parametric contrasts (prediction error, Q) but the paper does not report any contrasts that match risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it does not meet I5 and more broadly its task does not fit the review's target categories (E5). The study does include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (I6) and reports coordinates (I8), and participant groups are eligible (I7), but the absence of an admissible decision-making contrast leads to exclusion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (n=12) performing a perceptual decision task (random-dot motion coherence; saccade or button responses) (I4). The analyses explicitly include a perceptual difficulty factor (interaction between perceptual difficulty and time), indicating comparisons across difficulty levels (i.e., hard vs easy or low vs high coherence), satisfying the required decision-making contrast format for perceptual DM (I5). The reported results are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps (model fit and inference over whole brain, FDR voxel-level threshold p<0.05), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participant group is acceptable (healthy adults) (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in tables (Table 2) and text (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not resting/connectivity-only (E7), not baseline-only contrasts (E3), and it is empirical fMRI data (not E9). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets review objective and all inclusion criteria: the study used fMRI during a perceptual (2AFC) decision-making task (I4), reports within-task condition contrasts (Pos > Neut-P; Neg > Neut-N) comparing decision-making conditions (I5), and includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Analyses 2 and 3: second-level random-effects, whole-brain inference) with reported peaks (I6, I8). Participant sample and task type are acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and results are within-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a gambling (card-guessing) task that manipulated risk (choices between small likely vs large unlikely rewards), satisfying the review’s focus on risky decision-making. It reports within-subject contrasts directly comparing risk levels (e.g., Analysis 23810974_analysis_6: 6/7 > 1/7, high-risk > low-risk) and other risk-level contrasts (analyses 0,1,2,7,9). Group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain for multiple analyses; several results are FWE-corrected and reported as peak coordinates/tables). Participants are healthy humans (n=20). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest only), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are present (not ROI-only), and the task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded task types). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and the permissive reporting criterion I8; no exclusion criteria are met.

The study used fMRI in humans performing a decision-making task involving monetary reward probabilities (slot machines), manipulating uncertainty/risk (e.g., P=0.5 vs P=0.25). It reports within-task contrasts that compare higher vs lower uncertainty (e.g., P=0.5 > P=0.25), consistent with risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts. Analyses were estimated and inferred over the whole brain at the group level (voxelwise maps) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants are healthy human adults (n=31). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included.

This study used fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making) and reports a within-group contrast of IGT > control task (meets I4 and I5). Participants are human older adults (I7). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (VMPFC) with model fit and inference restricted to the ROI; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study does not meet the review's decision-making task criteria. The NeuroStore record shows only a visual stimulation (checkerboard) > rest contrast (no decision-making contrast of the types required). Although the abstract mentions probabilistic reversal learning (a cognitive flexibility task), it is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis, and the record does not provide qualifying contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. The record does satisfy I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise map present), I7 (healthy participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported), but these do not overcome the lack of a qualifying decision-making contrast. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual) applies.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human females performing a decision-making task that manipulates sexual risk (low vs high risk partners) and asks participants how likely they would be to have sex — an explicit risky decision-making contrast. The paper reports a within-task contrast comparing decision conditions (low risk > high risk), estimated with a whole-brain, random-effects group map and cluster-corrected inference (whole-brain inference, reported peak coordinates). Participants are healthy humans. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition-vs-condition risk contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical map), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: this is not a baseline-only contrast, not PET, not an excluded task type because it explicitly manipulates risk, and it reports whole-brain activation rather than ROI- or connectivity-only results. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI reversal-learning task comparing conditions that differ in outcome uncertainty (2-choice vs 4-choice) and contrasts condition-versus-condition (unexpected non-reinforcement > expected reinforcement) including an interaction testing greater effects in 4-choice than 2-choice. This matches the review’s focus on ambiguous decision-making (uncertainty-related contrasts) and uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met (task-based fMRI during decision-making; condition-vs-condition contrasts mapping onto uncertainty/ambiguous DM; whole-brain group results; participant sample acceptable; results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, empirical data present). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (so I4 is met) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I6), includes eligible participant groups (I7) and reports coordinates/tables (I8). However, none of the reported contrasts match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts specified in I5: reported contrasts are outcome- or feedback-related (reward > punishment, punishment > reward), behavioral switching, and correlations with motivation — not contrasts such as risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy. Therefore the required decision-making contrast criterion (I5) is not met. This places the study outside the meta-analysis scope; it examines reward receipt/learning/feedback processing rather than the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts, invoking exclusion criterion E5. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps (random-effects GLM; Talairach) as coordinate peaks, so it meets I4, I6, I7 and I8. However, all reported statistical maps are between-group contrasts (schizophrenia patients vs healthy controls) rather than within-subject condition-versus-condition or task-versus-control contrasts (e.g., risky > safe). The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or condition-comparison of interest. This violates exclusion criterion E8 and fails inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing choices between a certain immediate reward and larger risky rewards with explicit probabilities (risky decision-making). It provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise results (parametric modulations and contrasts) linking BOLD to the subjective value of the risky option and decision conflict, with reported peak coordinates and voxelwise thresholding—satisfying whole-brain evidence. Analyses include within-task decision-related contrasts (parametric value and conflict effects) that qualify as decision-making contrasts for risky-DM. Participants are healthy humans and reporting meets acceptable forms (tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task not risky, or baseline-only contrasts) apply.

Exclusion met: E6 (only ROI inference reported with no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map). Evidence: NeuroStore entry for the key decision contrast (exploratory > exploitative) shows 'Model fit over: whole brain' but 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' with FWE ROI thresholding; reported peaks appear to reflect ROI-based results rather than an unmasked whole-brain group map. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task — reversal learning/reward-guided decisions), I5 (a within-task contrast comparing decision types: exploratory > exploitative), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study reports a task that is a challenging visuo-spatial discrimination (compare images, identical vs different), which qualifies as a perceptual decision-making task (I4). The reported contrast (DFCB+ > DFCB−) is a within-task condition-vs-condition comparison (meets I5). The statistical model was fit and inference performed over the whole brain with voxel-level FDR thresholding and group-level analysis, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participants are human healthy adults (acceptable per I7). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical. Although the exact meaning of the DFCB+/DFCB− labels is not spelled out in the NeuroStore extract, the contrast is clearly a condition-versus-condition within the perceptual discrimination task, so inclusion criteria are met.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) experiment using a card-guessing gambling task (risky decision-making) with healthy human participants (n=26 reported in analyses). It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., previous computer-selected win > previous self-selected win/loss; self-selection vs computer-selection) that are condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise group-level GLMs with reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>baseline-only) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

The study used fMRI during a gambling (risky decision-making) task and included a clinical participant group (meets I4 and I7). However, the NeuroStore record reports only region-of-interest analyses (dACC and left dlPFC ROIs) with model fit over ROIs and does not provide any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. Moreover, the extracted analyses do not report a decision-making condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe) in a whole-brain format. Therefore the study fails the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I6) and the explicit contrast requirement (I5), and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI results reported). Based on these gaps, the study must be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using a perceptual decision-making (2AFC) task with a motivation manipulation (motivated vs neutral). It includes at least one condition-vs-condition contrast (motivated > neutral). A group-level, whole-brain, second-level random-effects activation analysis (motivated > neutral) is reported with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates (analysis_4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Although the paper also reports ROI and seed-based connectivity analyses, it additionally provides unmasked whole-brain activation results (not only ROI/connectivity), so exclusion criteria E6 and E7 do not apply. Participants (patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls) fall within acceptable groups. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and no exclusion criteria are met.

The Salience Attribution Test is a probabilistic reward-learning task in which cues differ in reward probability; participants performed the fMRI task and contrasts compare cue-types (high- vs low-probability and subjective high- vs low-probability), meeting the review’s decision-making manipulation. Several reported group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are present (e.g. analyses 4, 6, 7, 8 report whole-brain inference with FWE correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy volunteers (eligible per I7). Reporting of coordinates/peaks and whole-brain results is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not only ROI-only, not only baseline contrasts, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making meta-analysis.

Excluded because the task is an associative reward/punishment learning task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (violates inclusion I4/I5) and the reported analyses are ROI-restricted to a striatum/MTL mask with inference restricted to that mask (violates whole-brain requirement I6 and meets exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (eligible participant group: healthy humans). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5, I6, I8. Exclusion criteria applied: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results). Full text is complete for screening.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a one-dimensional perceptual categorization task with an uncertainty-response option, satisfying perceptual decision-making (I4). It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (Uncertainty > Correct, Correct > Uncertainty) and a parametric distance-to-bound (difficulty) modulation, meeting I5. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs with inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Tables), meeting I6 and I8. Participants are healthy humans (n=29), meeting I7. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening.

The task is a reversal-learning reinforcement task (Virtual Morris Water Maze with punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses), not an explicitly risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Thus it does not meet I4/I5. Although the study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (meets I6) and includes eligible participant groups (I7) and coordinate/peaks reporting (I8), its contrasts are focused on between-group comparisons and cross-subject regressions (ASPD+P vs ASPD-P, vs non-offenders; PCL-R correlations) with no reported unmasked within-group task activation map. Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (task not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and E8 (only between-group contrasts / interactions with no within-group task effect) are met. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

Excluded because the study reports only between-group/cross-subject regression analyses without a within-task condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/associations with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise model fit), I7 (participant groups are acceptable: substance users and controls), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task condition contrast or task > control contrast as required). Full text appears complete in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Thus excluded for failing I5 and meeting E8.

This study used fMRI while participants made decisions about taking medications that varied in side-effect probability and efficacy, which constitutes risky decision-making. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (Mild > Severe and Severe > Mild) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reported peak coordinates (tables). Healthy human participants were scanned. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain task-evoked maps, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only, non-risk task) apply.

The task is a conditioning/reinforcement two-choice prediction task manipulating error rates; this is not a clearly risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined for the meta-analysis. Although the paper reports a within-task contrast comparing decision-making conditions (20% > 80% error rate) and provides whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (coordinate table), the task appears to probe reinforcement/learning/error-driven adjustment rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (group comparisons and interactions) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation map reported, meeting exclusion criterion E8. The study does satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky decision-making task), I5 (risky > safe contrast present, albeit as an interaction), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (allowed participant groups), and I8 (coordinates reported). No other exclusion criteria apply. Based on the provided document, the lack of any within-group whole-brain task contrasts means the paper must be excluded per E8.

The study used an appropriate risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and reports between-group contrasts (e.g., Risky>Safe), so inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are satisfied. Participants are acceptable (I7). However, all reported analyses were conducted and inferred within predefined region-of-interest masks (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) and no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). Additionally, the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effects, meeting exclusion E8. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study (n=23) reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise contrasts from a risky decision-making task. The task manipulated behavioral risk and reward risk, and key contrasts include behavioral risk > certainty (i.e., risk > certainty) and reward-related contrasts; results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise peaks in tables. Thus it meets I4 (human fMRI risky decision-making task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrast: behavioral risk > certainty, an allowed risky-DM contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (coordinates/tables of whole-brain results provided). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are condition-vs-condition rather than only implicit-baseline, and the report contains empirical fMRI activation maps. Therefore include.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a two-choice perceptual decision task (2AFC) with human participants (n=24). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions differing in uncertainty/certainty (e.g., correct-unsure > correct-sure and sure > unsure), which match perceptual-DM contrast forms (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were fit and inference was performed over the whole brain for key contrasts (Analyses 26453582_analysis_0 and _1), with coordinates/peaks reported. Some analyses used ROI-restricted inference, but whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI results, task vs implicit baseline only) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

The study uses fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (predict which ball reaches first) and reports group-level whole-brain contrasts and coordinates, but the reported contrasts compare feedback valence (negative vs positive feedback, interaction with feedback presence) rather than decision difficulty/uncertainty or a perceptual task vs control. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participants are healthy adults, allowed), I8 (results reported as peak coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — no qualifying decision-making contrast of the accepted forms for perceptual DM (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, or perceptual task > control task). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

The study reports an fMRI task involving risk-related decision-making (sexual decisions with explicit risk information such as previous partners and condom use, and other risky items), includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., All low > All high; high vs low risk contrasts and interactions), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain thresholding. It is not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only, and includes an appropriate within-task contrast. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, with no exclusion criteria met.

The study used fMRI during a perceptual two-choice decision task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses, so I4 (fMRI perceptual decision task), I6 (whole-brain evidence), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results clearly reported) are satisfied. However, the reported contrasts are cross-subject regressions associating individual-difference diffusion-model parameters (drift rate, boundary separation) with BOLD activity rather than condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts (e.g., hard>easy or perceptual task>control) required by I5. No qualifying between-condition or task>control contrast is described. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered by the available document. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) study using the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making) with a within-task contrast decision > no decision and reported whole-brain peaks. Analysis metadata show a group-level whole-brain second-level model (one-way ANCOVA) and voxelwise thresholding for between-group tests; the within-task contrast (decision > no decision) is reported with 13 peaks, indicating whole-brain task-evoked results are available. The task and contrast meet risky-DM definitions. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and includes within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts (not only between-group effects). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study reports human fMRI during a probabilistic classification decision-making task, with within-task contrasts between decision conditions (High time pressure > Low time pressure) and multiple whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. These satisfy that (I4) an fMRI decision-making task was used, (I5) at least one condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast is reported (HighP > LowP and within-condition effects), and (I6) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are provided. Participants are healthy adults, so (I7) is met, and whole-brain results are reported as tables/peaks, satisfying (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), modality is fMRI, task is decision-making under uncertainty/time pressure (not an excluded paradigm), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports group-level, whole-brain fMRI of a risky decision-making task (coin gamble task) with explicit risky > sure (Risky Bet > Sure Bet) contrasts and between-group (age) comparisons. Analyses are voxelwise, cluster-corrected, and report peak coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The record also shows within-group task-related contrasts (gamble wins/losses). Participant samples (children, adolescents, adults) do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I8) are met; participant-group criterion I7 is not a barrier. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports an fMRI visual motion coherence discrimination task (perceptual decision-making) with group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts. It includes parametric modulation by coherence (positive and negative parametric effects), which constitutes within-task comparisons of perceptual difficulty (analogous to low-coherence > high-coherence or hard > easy). Task analyses (group-mean one-sample t-tests) were fit and inferred over the whole brain and peak coordinates are reported. Participants are healthy humans and results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM task), I5 (within-task contrasts by coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain task maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-only; not baseline-only contrasts).

The study reports a 7T fMRI task that includes ambiguous, unambiguous, and incongruent sequence conditions and tests within-subject contrasts between these decision-making conditions (e.g., A21 > U221, A21 > I212). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and peak coordinates are reported (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain for key contrasts; reported peaks). Participants are healthy humans (n=22). These features satisfy the review’s requirement for an fMRI study of ambiguous decision-making with condition-versus-condition contrasts and whole-brain group results. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline, this is not PET, whole-brain results are provided (not only ROI or connectivity), and within-group task contrasts are present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria.

This study reports event-related fMRI during a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Bad > Good) satisfying the risky-DM contrast forms. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; FDR-corrected maps; reported peak coordinates). Participant groups include substance-dependent and non-dependent humans, which are acceptable. Results include within-task condition contrasts and cross-subject regressions rather than only baseline contrasts or ROI/connectivity-only results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study used the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (MIDT), which is an anticipatory/reward-processing task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. The reported contrasts (e.g., A1W > A1N, A1L > A1N, A2L > A2N) compare prospect (reward/loss) vs neutral conditions, not decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy. Thus it does not meet the core task/contrast requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual decision-making). fulltext_incomplete=false

Exclusion E5 met: the task is a probabilistic reinforcement/feedback learning (instrumental conditioning) focused on reward vs punishment sensitivity and menstrual-cycle modulation, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported; model fit over whole brain and peak tables), I7 (healthy human participants qualify), I8 (results reported in tables/peaks as acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrasts of the accepted forms for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM — contrasts are feedback valence and cycle-phase interactions rather than risk>safe, ambiguity contrasts, or hard>easy perceptual comparisons). Therefore the study is excluded per E5.

This study collected fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) in humans (n=77) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and contrasts. The NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fit and inference, thresholding, and tables of peak coordinates (Analyses 0 and 4), plus task regressors and parametric modulators indexing risk/reward and PPI psychological regressors for risk and reward—supporting within-task condition contrasts beyond implicit baseline. The task is a canonical risky-DM paradigm, satisfying the review objective. No exclusion criteria (PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, baseline-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI BOLD investigation using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) performed by human participants, satisfying I4. It includes within-task parametric modulation analyses of explosion (risk) probabilities (within-group associations) and between-condition contrasts related to inflation/success events, which provide comparisons across levels of risk (qualifying as risky-DM contrasts), satisfying I5. Model fitting and inference were performed voxelwise over the whole brain and results are reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups (patients and healthy controls; males aged within eligible range) are acceptable, satisfying I7. Although several reported contrasts are between-group, the study also reports unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects (parametric modulations), so it does not meet exclusion E8. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are met. Overall, the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study uses fMRI in human participants performing a task with explicit reward probabilities (Monetary Incentive Delay) and reports within-task contrasts that compare different probability conditions (e.g., 25–100% > 0%, and positive vs negative prediction error). These contrasts constitute condition-vs-condition comparisons of risk/uncertainty consistent with risky decision-making contrasts. Models were fit over the whole brain and group-level inference (FWE-corrected and uncorrected voxel/cluster thresholds) is reported with peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy humans and results are reported in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria (PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

The task is a two-stage (two-step) reinforcement-learning task probing model-based vs model-free control, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required (I4 not met). Reported contrasts are reward-prediction-error parametric modulations and between-group comparisons (e.g., RPE ΔMB relapsers < abstainers/HCs) rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy (I5 not met). The study does report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (Analysis 0: whole-brain inference) so I6 is met; participant eligibility is acceptable (I7 met); and whole-brain results are reported (I8 met). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) applies. Full text was available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) risky decision-making task in human participants (n=22) with within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., Gain>Loss, Accept>Reject, risk-related contrasts). Multiple analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (analyses 5–11 report FWE-corrected, whole-brain inferences with reported peak coordinates/tables). Results are reported in tables of peaks. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria for a risky decision-making fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level contrasts are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E8 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction (group × outcome) contrast (IGD after loss > HC after win) with whole-brain inference, and does not report any unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task activation maps. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — BART), I5 (contrast compares decision-making conditions: post-outcome risk-related activation), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because the paper provides only between-group/interaction results with no accompanying whole-brain within-group task effects, it must be excluded per E8.

This fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (virtual sexual 'hook up') in human participants and reports contrasts such as Risky-sex > Safe-sex (I4 and I5 satisfied). Participants are acceptable (I7) and results are reported in extracted tables/peaks (I8). However, all reported analyses were region-of-interest (insula) with model fit and inference restricted to that ROI; no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map is reported. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I6. Exclusion IDs met: E6.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed perceptual decision-making (2AFC) tasks (I4). The paper includes within-group parametric contrasts linking uncertainty levels to BOLD activity (criterion comparison and signal-detection parametric modulations), which correspond to decision-making comparisons of high vs low uncertainty (qualifying under I5). Analyses are group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates reported (I6, I8). Participant sample is acceptable (I7). The contrasts are condition-versus-condition/parametric (not task>rest or implicit baseline), and results are not limited to ROI, PET, connectivity-only, or between-group-only contrasts, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and should be included.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI conducted during gambling/risky decision-making tasks), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 — the paper does not report a decision-making contrast that compares decision conditions (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk) or an experimental decision task > control task. The reported contrasts are reward > no reward and anticipation, which index outcome receipt/anticipation rather than risk-related decision contrasts required by the meta-analysis. Therefore the study fails to meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

The study reports group-level, whole-brain fMRI contrasts that directly compare uncertainty conditions (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty) which match the ambiguous decision-making contrast form in I5. The task involves detection/response decisions under varying uncertainty (perceptual/ambiguous decision context), and multiple within-group contrasts (TERM>EXT, EXT>TERM, CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW, SURPRISE) are reported. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain with voxelwise inference/cluster correction and peak coordinates are reported in tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy human adults (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), it is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain task activations are reported (not only ROI or connectivity-only), and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The paper reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts (control > stroke overall and control > stroke for smiley feedback) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails to provide the required within-task decision-making contrast (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic classification decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening. Given these facts, the study should be excluded.

This study reports fMRI of human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices with explicitly stated 50% win probability between social interaction and monetary amounts), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (decoding/contrast risky > safe), satisfying I5. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (Analysis 1: whole-brain model fit and whole-brain voxelwise FWE inference), satisfying I6. Participants are healthy humans and within acceptable age range (I7). Results/peaks are reported (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: not PET (E4), contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline (not E3), whole-brain task activations are reported (not E6 or E7), and contrasts include within-group task effects (not E8). Although the task has a social component, it involves explicit risk (50% chance) and appropriate risky > safe contrasts, so it fits the risky decision-making inclusion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (I4). It reports within-task contrasts/parametric modulations related to risk and missed opportunities (within-group parametric contrasts), which count as decision-making condition contrasts (I5). Group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects models were estimated over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain; Analysis 2 shows whole-brain voxelwise results and reported peaks), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participants are healthy humans within eligible ages (I7). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates and described (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only task>rest, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study is excluded because it uses delay discounting (intertemporal choice) and probability discounting; delay/intertemporal tasks are explicitly excluded per E5. While the task includes a probabilistic component, the paper’s primary paradigm is delay/probability discounting (title and task: Delay and Probability Discounting), and many reported contrasts are parametric modulations of subjective value rather than condition-vs-condition risk contrasts required by I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task — probability discounting constitutes risky DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain models reported; model fit over whole brain and voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast such as “risky > safe” or “hard > easy” or task>control). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is delay/intertemporal discounting, which the review excludes). Therefore exclude.

Decision: EXCLUDE based on E5. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 - the task is a model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning Markov decision task and not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Analyses focus on computational regressors (state prediction error, reward prediction error) rather than contrasts of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported/triaged into tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task does not clearly fall into the review's risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making categories), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy; instead parametric learning signals were reported). Therefore the study is not eligible for this meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a two-choice gambling (risky decision-making) task (meets I4). It reports within-group, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts indexing response proportional to risk magnitude during the choice phase (parametric modulation/high-risk vs low-risk type contrast), fulfilling the required decision-making contrast form (I5). Models were fit over the whole brain and inference was conducted at the group (2nd-level) whole-brain level with reported peak coordinates (meets I6 and I8). Participants were healthy humans (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), not PET, not ROI-only, and not connectivity-only. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study involves human participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement (passive avoidance) task (I4) and reports whole-brain group-level task maps (analyses 3–7) with peaks in tables (I6, I8). Participants are an acceptable group (maltreated children and controls) (I7). However, the extracted analyses report only between-group contrasts (MT > NMT or NMT > MT) for parametric regressors (EV, PE) and ROI results; there is no evidence in the NeuroStore record of any within-group, unmasked whole-brain contrasts that directly compare two decision-making conditions of interest (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy) or a task > control contrast. Thus the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect, which meets exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criterion I5 (required contrast comparing decision-making conditions) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Exclusion rationale:
(a) Exclusion IDs met: None (no exclusion criteria from the list are triggered).
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a gambling/risky decision-making Card-Guessing task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant ages within eligible range), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate peaks/tables).
(c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5. The paper does not report any contrast that compares two decision-making conditions of interest for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual hard>easy). Fulltext_incomplete: false.

The study reports an fMRI experiment (bold response) in healthy human participants performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task, satisfying I4. It provides within-task, between-condition contrasts indexing decision processes (outcomes that increased vs reduced risk-seeking), which meet I5’s requirement for condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and group-level contrasts reported as coordinate tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample and age are acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and contrasts are not task>rest only. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion applied: E8 (study reports only between-group/interaction whole-brain contrasts with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (task-based fMRI during an Instrumental Conditioning Task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported for omnibus contrasts), I7 (participant group acceptable — MDD patients), I8 (coordinates/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no clearly reported decision-making contrast comparing two decision conditions or task vs active control of the form required for risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM; contrasts reported are omnibus/group interactions or treatment/time comparisons rather than e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Therefore exclude. Full text appears complete enough for screening.

This study uses fMRI during a risky decision-making task and reports whole-brain, group-level maps, but it does not provide an unambiguous within-group contrast that directly compares two decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe) or a task-versus-control contrast. The reported statistical maps are primarily between-group contrasts/interactions (e.g., CS > OSU, interaction contrasts) and cross-subject regression associations; no clear within-group risky>safe (or equivalent) contrast is present in the NeuroStore record. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear contrast comparing two decision-making conditions). Full text is available in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used fMRI during a Card-Guessing (gambling) task (I4) and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts comparing uncertainty/risk levels (e.g., 50% > 100%; 87.5%; 75%; 62.5%), which match risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts (I5). The reported analysis is a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analysis (FLAME) with model fit over the whole brain and thresholded clusters reported (I6). Participant groups (adolescents with anxiety and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are reported with peaks/coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not only ROI or connectivity), and the reported effects are not limited to only between-group contrasts without within-task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study tested human participants performing a risky driving decision task (urgent vs evaluative behaviors), with within-subject contrasts comparing two decision-making conditions (urgent > evaluative and evaluative > urgent). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (single-sample t-tests; model fit over whole brain; voxel- and cluster-level thresholds; coordinates/peaks provided). Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text is available in the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a gambling/card-guessing decision task that manipulated decision rule complexity and decision certainty (choice/outcome certainty). It reports multiple within-subject contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions (e.g., low choice certainty > high choice certainty; complex rule-based > probabilistic choice) rather than task>baseline, and results are derived from whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with peak coordinates reported. Participants are human (n=15). These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not a non-empirical paper).

The study uses fMRI during a probabilistic classification task that manipulates uncertainty (meets I4) and reports entropy-related contrasts/parametric effects relevant to ambiguous decision-making (meets I5). Participants are an eligible human sample (meets I7) and results/peaks are reported (meets I8). However, the reported uncertainty/decision-related analyses (e.g. positive correlation with entropy during the delay; entropy modulation contrasts) were conducted and inferred within a midbrain region-of-interest (SN/VTA ROI) with no evidence in this document of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Because the decision-related effects are only reported from an ROI and no whole-brain group maps are provided, the study fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and thus falls under exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses reported). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study used fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination), satisfying I4. It reports within-group condition contrasts (face > house and house > face), which are condition-versus-condition decision-making contrasts acceptable under I5. Multiple analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with reported peak coordinates (Analyses 0,1,3,4,5), meeting I6 and I8. Participants are healthy humans, so I7 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not only versus implicit baseline (E3), the modality is fMRI not PET (E4), the task is perceptual decision-making (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (not E6), and the study is empirical (not E9). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

E5: The reported task is a multidimensional probabilistic reinforcement-learning (multi-armed bandit) task and the reported contrasts are parametric prediction-error correlations. The study does not report any of the decision-making contrasts specified in I5 (e.g., risky>safe; high uncertainty>low uncertainty; hard>easy) nor a task-versus-active-control contrast. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported). Inclusion not met: I4 (the task is reinforcement learning/multidimensional learning rather than a clearly defined risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the review definitions) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study used fMRI with a task that required ambiguous perceptual/emotion judgments (consonance/dissonance), and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Intermediate Dissonance > Consonance). However, the critical decision-making contrasts were reported with inference restricted to a region-of-interest (small-volume correction). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported only for task>baseline contrasts (sound > baseline), which are not acceptable as the sole decision-related contrasts for the meta-analysis. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for the relevant decision-making contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (within-task condition contrasts such as ambiguous > non-ambiguous), I7 (participant sample acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level statistical map reported for the decision-making contrasts of interest). No exclusion criteria from the list apply exactly. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI risky decision-making task with whole-brain, group-level results but the NeuroStore record shows only a between-group contrast (high vs low TAS) / group-by-condition interaction. Exclusion E8 applies: the paper appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain inference reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/table). Inclusion criterion I5 is not met in the available document because there is no unmasked, whole-brain within-group contrast comparing two decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe) reported—only the between-group interaction is shown. Therefore the study must be excluded under E8.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a risky gambling task (choices between low- and high-risk options with varying probabilities), satisfying I4. It reports within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions (decision-for-self vs decision-for-other) and parametric modulations tied to probability of making risky choices, meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain GLMs were estimated and peak coordinates are reported (model fit over whole brain; coordinates listed), and results are described in the text/abstract, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample (healthy adults) meets I7. Although several reported inferences used small-volume correction (ROIs), the study nonetheless used whole-brain GLMs and reports voxelwise peaks rather than only ROI statistics, and connectivity/parametric analyses include whole-brain fits, so exclusion for ROI-only reporting (E6) does not apply. No exclusion criteria (E3,E4,E5,E6,E7,E8,E9) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The paper reports fMRI during decision-making (probabilistic/risky and delay discounting) with whole-brain, group-level GLM results and coordinate tables, but ALL reported contrasts in the NeuroStore record are between-group interactions (IGD vs RGU vs HC) and no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (e.g., probability>certain or delay>no-delay within a single group) is reported. This violates exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (probabilistic discounting constitutes risky decision-making), I5 (task contrasts compare decision-making conditions such as probability>fixed/certain and delay>no-delay), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: none of the listed inclusion criteria are absent, but because the paper reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying within-group unmasked whole-brain task effect, it must be excluded per E8.

This study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune), but the reported group-level analysis is an ROI-based between-group interaction (Boys > Girls for Win > No Win) with inference restricted to an a priori nucleus accumbens ROI. Exclusion criteria E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) is met. Also, only a between-group interaction contrast is reported with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect, meeting E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (requires whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) is not satisfied; I5 (requires an admissible decision-making contrast form such as risky>safe or similar) is not clearly satisfied because the reported contrast is reward feedback (win>no win) as a between-group interaction rather than an accepted risky>safe type contrast. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study used an fMRI reversal-learning/probabilistic reward-guided task and reports only prediction-error and between-group contrasts (HC>ADP, interactions) rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Although whole-brain group-level PE contrasts are reported, the report contains only between-group contrasts and interactions with no unmasked whole-brain within-group decision-task effect described. Therefore it does not meet the required decision-making contrast specification (I5) and falls outside the review’s target task types (E5). It also violates exclusion E8 (only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect). I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. Excluded for not meeting inclusion I5 and for meeting exclusion E5 and E8.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (judging spatial frequency of Gabor patches) and reports group-level, whole-brain maps (FWE-thresholded, MNI coordinates). However, the NeuroStore record only documents between-group contrasts/interactions (age x orientation interaction; older > younger for same orientation) and does not report any within-group, unmasked whole-brain task contrast of decision difficulty (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence) or a decision-versus-control contrast. Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts with no accompanying whole-brain within-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no documented decision-condition vs decision-condition or task-vs-control contrast in the record). Therefore the study is excluded under E8.

The study reports fMRI during a risky decision-making task (I4). It includes group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps: several parametric modulation and contrast analyses were fit over the whole brain (Analyses 0–4, 5–6 include whole-brain voxelwise regressions), providing voxelwise results (MNI coordinates and reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6, I8).
