The paper contains decision-related contrasts/analyses that map onto the admissible risky-DM forms—e.g., positive correlation with experienced risk (parametric modulation/high-risk > low-risk analogue) and risky > safe comparisons (analyses reported, including ROI but whole-brain parametric effects are present), meeting the contrast requirement (I5). Participants are human and acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not only against baseline, not PET, task is risky DM, whole-brain results are reported (so not E3–E6, E7, E8, E9). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual/risky decision task (choosing between lotteries with explicit probabilities and voltage/payoff levels) with BOLD measured (I4). Reported contrasts are within-task probability-sensitive effects (positive and negative correlations with probability across levels 1/6–1), which constitute condition-vs-condition, within-group decision-making contrasts (meets I5). The model was fit over the whole brain and peaks are reported in MNI coordinates (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample is within acceptable groups (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not task>rest only (E3), not connectivity-only (E7), not between-group-only (E8), and it is empirical (not E9). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusions.

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) model fitting and presents only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task activation map. Specifically, exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results) and E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (contains an ambiguous > non-ambiguous between-group contrast matching the admitted ambiguous-DM contrast forms) and I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task appears to be instruction-based learning/outcome integration rather than a clear risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps; model fit over ROI). Fulltext appears complete.

Excluded because the study’s task is social/emotional judgment (approach/avoid of faces), which is social decision-making rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criterion E5 applies. Although the paper reports group-level fMRI with whole-brain model fitting and reported peaks (satisfying I6, I7, and I8), it does not include any contrasts of the admitted forms for risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4 and I5 are not met). No other exclusion criteria appear to apply. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s topic-specific inclusion requirements and is excluded.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level results and coordinate peaks. However, the NeuroStore record shows only omnibus between-group contrasts/interactions (GROUP×BEHAVIOR; GROUP×CONDITION) and no within-group task contrasts or condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts of the types required (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task not clearly an admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM contrast per the review’s operationalization) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrasts). Hence the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study used a perceptual decision-making task (face gender categorization) with BOLD measures in humans (n=16). It reports within-subject, condition-versus-condition whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., N-p > N-a, N-p > C), which are task-vs-task comparisons analogous to perceptual difficulty contrasts (noise/degraded > intact). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates (tables), meeting the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied.

The study reports fMRI data collected during a probabilistic classification (weather prediction) decision-making task (I4). It includes relevant within-task and task-vs-control contrasts (WPT task > control task; high vs low predictive trials; feedback contrasts) satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast (I5). The analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise maps with FDR voxel-level correction and coordinates reported in Talairach tables (I6, I8). Participants are healthy humans (age range overlaps inclusion; participant characteristics do not exclude the study per I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not only task>rest baseline (E3), not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7), and include within-group contrasts (not only between-group) (E8). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task with parametric modulation of risk. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLMs were fit and whole-brain inference was performed; peak coordinates are reported in tables. The parametric risk regressor constitutes a within-task contrast indexing greater response to higher vs lower risk (equivalent to high-risk > low-risk), satisfying the required contrast types. Results are reported as whole-brain task-evoked maps (coordinate tables), and participants are within the accepted population. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making whole-brain fMRI evidence and should be included.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is a social Trust Game (social decision-making), which is explicitly listed among excluded task types. Included criteria met: I5 (the paper reports decision-task vs control contrasts: Fair>Control, Unfair>Control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study directly examines risky decision-making (mixed gain/loss gambles) during scanning and reports within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of gain–loss ratios, quadratic effects) and between-group contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain model fitting and several inferences explicitly reported over the whole brain (FWE cluster-level corrected results and reported peak coordinates/tables). Participants include pathological gamblers and healthy controls; results are reported as peaks/tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study used a perceptual judgment task (tactile texture ratings) and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (peaks/tables) in both within-group and between-group analyses, the reported task contrasts are only task-versus-rest (e.g., Mesh > baseline/rest). The review’s inclusion requires a condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast for perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard>easy, perceptual task>control). No such condition-vs-condition or active control contrasts are reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/rest) is met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast).

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain task data during a probabilistic reversal-learning task and a Tower of London planning task (I4, I6). Participants include patients and controls and results are reported in tables (I7, I8). However, the reported task contrasts are primarily condition-versus-baseline/neutral-feedback (e.g., “monetary loss followed by reversal > baseline; neutral feedback”) and multiple reported results are between-group interactions rather than the within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore the study does not provide an eligible decision-making contrast per I5 and its contrasts against implicit baseline violate exclusion criterion E3. Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

This study reports fMRI (BOLD) during a gambling task (risky decision-making) and includes multiple within-task condition contrasts comparing risk levels (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; 6 in 7 > 1 in 7). Analyses were fit and inference conducted at the whole-brain, group level with reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are human healthy adults. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (risky decision-making, condition-vs-condition contrasts, whole-brain group maps, acceptable participant groups, and coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a Card-Guessing (Gambling) Task involving monetary bets and anticipation of reward, which constitutes a risky decision-making paradigm. The report lists within-group, omnibus contrasts with gambling condition terms and first-level analyses, and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (MNI coordinates, reported peak tables), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are an acceptable group and results are reported in coordinate tables. Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts implied by gambling condition/anticipation of reward contrasts and reported peaks), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/ connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts).

Meets fMRI risky decision-making criteria: task involves bluffing with potential loss (risky choice) and the abstract and analysis state the amygdala responded preferentially following the risky choice. The NeuroStore extraction reports a within-group contrast labeled “nonmatch” (a decision-related contrast) with results reported as voxelwise whole-brain GLM peaks (Model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks: 2), satisfying requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map. Participants are healthy humans (n=12, ages 18–46). Results are reported as peaks (coordinates), which is acceptable. Notes: the group model used fixed effects and sample size is small, but neither is listed as exclusionary. Therefore all inclusion criteria required are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI during valuation tasks and reports coordinates (I4, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the reported analysis is a searchlight multivariate decoding restricted to predefined ROIs (model fit/inference restricted to searchlights within literature-defined regions) and does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (violates I6). The primary reported contrast is an omnibus comparison differentiating probabilistic (risky) versus intertemporal valuation rather than a standard risky-vs-safe or task-vs-control contrast specified in the inclusion rules (I5 not met). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Conclusion: EXCLUDE. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making Random Dot Kinematogram task (I4); reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., R75/25 > NR75/25) comparing decision-making conditions rather than baseline (I5); provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps/peak coordinates with conventional thresholding (FDR and cluster thresholds) (I6); participants are healthy humans within eligible age ranges (I7); and whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinate tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not PET, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, and include within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with human participants (n=22). It includes at least one within-subject decision-related contrast (a parametric modulation of ‘increasing conformity’) that was tested at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise inference (second-level random-effects one-sample t-test; FDR thresholding). These features satisfy the review’s requirements for (I4) fMRI during a perceptual decision task, (I5) a within-task decision-making contrast, (I6) whole-brain group-level results, (I7) an acceptable participant group, and (I8) acceptable reporting of results. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI, not task>baseline only, not connectivity-only, empirical fMRI activations present). Full text is complete as represented here.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) in human participants (n=23) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects) with cluster-based FWE correction. Reported contrasts include within-task parametric modulations related to decision variables (trial-wise acquired bias and coherence-related regressors and RPEs), which constitute within-task decision-making contrasts relevant to perceptual DM. Whole-brain results are provided as peak coordinates/tables. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state/only connectivity; not baseline-only contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making whole-brain evidence and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making Wheel of Fortune task (I4) and includes healthy adolescent participants (I7). However, the reported analysis is a between-group interaction (HSS > LSS: Win vs No Win) tested within a region-of-interest only (model fit and inference restricted to ROI). No whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map is reported in this record. Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and is excluded under E6 (ROI-only with no whole-brain results). Additionally, the only reported contrast is a between-group interaction with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect, meeting E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (contrast is outcome receipt vs omission, not a decision-making condition contrast as required) and I6 (no whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria applied: E6, E8.

The study reports an fMRI reversal-learning task (meets I4) in human participants (meets I7) but the reported analyses are ROI-based and report only omnibus between-group contrasts. Model fit was over regions of interest (ACC, VS, vmPFC) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, and the extracted contrasts are omnibus between-group comparisons rather than within-task decision-vs-decision or task-vs-control contrasts. Therefore the study violates the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain task activation maps and for availability of within-task decision contrasts. Exclusion IDs applied: E6 (only ROI analyses) and E8 (only between-group contrasts with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I4, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6.

This study used fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task, a risky decision-making task, and tested a condition factor contrasting high-risk versus low-risk decisions within a group-level, voxelwise ANOVA. The model was fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level task-evoked whole-brain results. The report includes condition contrasts (high-risk vs low-risk) rather than task vs rest. Participants include clinical and healthy groups (eligible populations). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only results, task vs baseline only contrasts) are met. Note: inference was SVC-corrected in some regions, but the model was estimated whole-brain and coordinates are reported, so the study provides usable whole-brain activation evidence for risky decision-making.

The task is an antisaccade (inhibitory control) paradigm with reward manipulation, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (fails I4 and I5). The NeuroStore record indicates all reported contrasts are omnibus between-group comparisons (adolescents vs adults) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation maps described, so this meets exclusion E8. The study does report group-level whole-brain analyses (analyses 3,5,9) and coordinate tables (satisfying I6 and I8) and includes an allowable participant sample (I7). However because the task does not meet the review’s decision-making domain (I4/I5 not met) and the results appear limited to between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked within-group whole-brain task effect (E8), the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study used a perceptual decision-making task (perceptual curiosity with blurred vs clear images), satisfying I4. It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (FIRST PICTURE BLURRED > FIRST PICTURE CLEAR; SECOND PICTURE B–C corresponding > B–C unrelated), matching allowed perceptual contrasts (hard/ambiguous > easy/non-ambiguous), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported (Analyses 2 and 3: model fit over whole brain; third-level mixed-effects group analyses), satisfying I6. Participants are healthy humans (I7). Whole-brain peaks/coordinates are reported in tables, acceptable per I8. Although some ROI-restricted analyses are reported, the presence of whole-brain group results means E6 does not apply. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study reports fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning decision-making task (decisions under uncertainty), meeting the review’s task domain. It includes within-task contrasts and condition comparisons (e.g., positive vs negative prediction errors; both rewarding conditions > both punishment conditions), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise maps with FWE-corrected inference and peaks reported in tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are human and acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only baseline contrasts). Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion.

This fMRI study used a gambling task contrasting safe (sure) vs gamble choices and reports a group-level (second-level) within-subject interaction contrast involving decision type (gamble vs sure) and conditioned stimuli. Analysis 1 was fit over the whole brain and reports voxelwise peaks (p<0.005 voxel-level), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. The task is a risky decision-making paradigm (safe vs gamble), participants are human, and results include reported peaks (coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), this is fMRI (not PET), and whole-brain results are reported in addition to an ROI analysis. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic card-guessing (gambling) task manipulating uncertainty (50% vs 100% predictive probabilities). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Talairach coordinates, voxel-level thresholding) including within-group contrasts (50%>100%) and between-group comparisons, with peaks reported in tables. These contrasts directly map onto ambiguous/risky decision-making comparisons (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts, e.g., 50%>100%), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, includes within-group effects). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used task-based fMRI in humans while participants made explicit risk judgments about scenarios (risky decision-making). It reports within-subject contrasts that directly compare decision conditions (e.g., High Risk > Low Risk; High Harm > Low Harm) rather than task-versus-baseline. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects tests (voxelwise ANOVA; whole-brain inference; reported peak coordinates/tables). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI whole-brain contrasts are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the task and reported contrasts do not meet the review's decision-making domain and contrast requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the task is a reversal learning/feedback learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and E8 (the NeuroStore record reports only omnibus between-group/interactions contrasts with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported). Full text appears complete in the record. Given these mismatches, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study (n=23) used a gambling/risky decision-making task (Card-Guessing) while acquiring BOLD fMRI data, directly addressing risky decision-making. It reports within-group, group-level random-effects contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., gamble > sure) and parametric modulators of variance and skewness. Several analyses indicate whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (FWE-corrected) and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts vs baseline only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal learning task, but the only extracted group-level result is a seed-based gPPI connectivity contrast (recAN > HC) for the lose-shift condition. Exclusion criteria E7 applies because the report contains only seed-based/effective connectivity analysis without a reported whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Exclusion criterion E8 also applies: the documented result is a between-group contrast with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect reported in this document. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task) and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast of the required forms is reported), I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map reported). Based on these mismatches, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not test the forms of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making required by the review. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (the task is diagnostic reasoning/medical decision-making and not a clearly defined risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as specified by the meta-analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable; healthy adults), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (unclear: although the study manipulates diagnosticity/uncertainty, the task is diagnostic reasoning and not explicitly categorized as risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM per review definitions), I5 (no reported contrast matching the required forms such as ambiguous > non-ambiguous, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, risky > safe, or hard > easy). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is excluded because analyses were fit and inference were restricted to a region-of-interest (ROI) and thresholding used small-volume correction, indicating no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map was reported (meets exclusion E6). The paper also reports only group x condition interaction/between-group contrasts with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect available (meets exclusion E8). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic decision-making task — weather prediction), I5 (task > active perceptual-motor control contrast reported), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map). Full text is complete for screening per provided record.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-related functional connectivity analyses (amygdala and NAcc) and diffusion (FA) group differences, without any unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation contrast of decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (only seed-based connectivity/effective/resting-state analyses with no whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (reports only between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I7 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-task condition contrasts such as risky>safe or task>control) and I6 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the paper does not provide the required task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the reported analyses are restricted to region-of-interest (ROI) model fitting and inference rather than unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (exclusion E6). Although the study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (meets I4), the document does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast such as hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or task>control (I5 not met), nor does it provide whole-brain voxelwise group results (I6 not met). The paper reports cross-subject regressions and peaks within anatomically or atlas-defined ROIs and lacks an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (also satisfying E8). Therefore it fails the whole-brain requirement and related inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study used an fMRI reversal-learning task and reports whole-brain, coordinate-based results, and participants include clinical groups acceptable to the review. However, reversal learning is not one of the meta-analysis target tasks (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and the reported contrasts are primarily between-group comparisons (patients vs. controls) and interactions rather than the within-task condition contrasts required (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion criteria E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete in this record.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky sequential investment (trust/stock) decision-making task, reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results. The paper reports whole-brain parametric modulation contrasts (TD error and Q-value modulators) relevant to decision variables in risky decision-making, which qualify as within-task decision-related contrasts. Coordinates/peaks are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This study investigates a delay discounting (intertemporal choice) task (choices between immediate and delayed rewards). The meta-analysis includes only risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks; delay discounting is explicitly excluded (E5). The paper does report group-level, whole-brain fMRI task contrasts (whole-brain inference and reported peaks), and includes acceptable participant groups and reporting formats. Therefore I apply inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain evidence), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). However it does not meet I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) nor I5 (accepted contrast types for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not one of the eligible DM types — delay discounting) is met, so the study must be excluded.

The study reports fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement learning (instrumental conditioning) task with whole-brain group analyses, but the reported contrasts are feedback-related parametric modulations (e.g., negative feedback modulated by RT-change, unsigned/negative prediction error). There are no contrasts that match the meta-analysis’ required decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Thus it fails the key inclusion criterion I5, and the task/contrasts do not clearly fit the meta-analysis categories of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (exclusion E5). Whole-brain results are present (satisfies I6), participants are an eligible group (I7), and results are reported as coordinates/tables (I8). Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a risky decision-making (card-guessing/gambling) task and neural responses to decision variables (e.g., accumulated reward, accept vs reject interactions) were tested. Analyses are within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference (FDR thresholding). The contrasts include within-task condition comparisons (e.g., accept-related interaction and parametric modulators tied to decision variables), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts. Participants are healthy humans. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed a monetary gambling (risky decision-making) task with multiple probability levels. The reported whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses include voxelwise parametric contrasts for probability (p) and a nonlinear deviation term Δ(p)×u(x), with coordinates and thresholding provided (tables of peaks). These contrasts constitute within-task, condition-versus-condition (parametric risk) effects rather than task>baseline contrasts. The sample, task, and analyses therefore meet the meta-analysis definitions for risky decision-making, whole-brain voxelwise maps, and reporting of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study does not provide a qualifying whole-brain fMRI task activation map for a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast. The NeuroStore record shows electrophysiological (FRN/ERP) analyses and a between-group contrast (learners > non-learners) in response to reward feedback; no within-task, unmasked whole-brain fMRI decision-making contrasts are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (only between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during a qualifying decision-making task reported in the extracted analyses), I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrast such as risky>safe, hard>easy, etc.), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked fMRI map available in the record). Hence excluded.

The study used fMRI during an approach-avoidance task with probabilistic threat levels, so it meets I4 (fMRI during decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrasts across CS threat levels), and I7/I8 (eligible participant group and coordinate reporting). However, all reported group analyses were fit and tested only within an AAL region-of-interest mask (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest; SVC reported). No unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map is reported. This fails inclusion criterion I6 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Consequently the study is excluded.

This study reports a human fMRI experiment (BOLD) with within-subject condition contrasts (congruent > control; incongruent > control; switch > non-switch control) that compare task conditions against an active control, and the task requires perceptual selection between stimulus pairs (number comparison/selection) consistent with perceptual decision-making. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with standard thresholding reported. Participants are human and eligible. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis scope (perceptual decision-making), provides appropriate condition-versus-control contrasts, and reports whole-brain results.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts directly comparing ambiguous versus clear stimuli (Analysis 29771359_analysis_1: Ambiguous > Clear; analysis_0: Clear > Ambiguous). The task is an event-related forced-choice categorization of prosodic expressions with explicitly ambiguous tokens, so the Ambiguous > Clear contrast corresponds to the meta-analysis ambiguous decision-making contrast (I5). Whole-brain random-effects inference was performed (I6). The study involves fMRI during a decision/categorization task (I4) and reports results in tables/peaks (I8); participant sample meets allowable groups (I7). It is not excluded by E3, E6, or E7 because it includes condition-vs-condition whole-brain task activations (not only baseline contrasts, ROI-only results, or connectivity-only findings). Although stimuli have social content, the critical contrast indexes perceptual/ambiguity-based decision-making rather than social-choice processes, so E5 does not apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study collected fMRI during a decision-making task that included probabilistic outcomes and effort costs, and reports whole-brain group contrasts and coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with a risk component present), I5 (within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (healthy participants acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: none of the required inclusion criteria are strictly unmet. However, exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study’s primary manipulation and reported contrasts focus on effort-based choice/effort costs (the paper emphasizes devaluation by physical effort and contrasts such as effortful vs effortless secured reward), and the paper’s aim is behavioral inconsistency in effort-based decisions rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. E5 (effort-based choice is excluded) therefore disqualifies the study from this meta-analysis.

The study acquired fMRI during a maze-navigation task that explicitly required sequential decision-making under uncertainty (resolution of uncertainty), meeting I4. The reported analysis is a within-group, whole-brain parametric modulation (distance to goal) that indexes uncertainty/resolution during decision-making, which constitutes an acceptable within-task decision-making contrast (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty), meeting I5. The model was fit over the whole brain and inference was performed over the whole brain at the group level, satisfying I6. Participant sample is within acceptable populations and ages (I7). Results are reported in the NeuroStore record with coordinates/peaks (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET study, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study investigates social risk perception in purchase decisions (anticipated social disapproval) using parametric modulation of social-risk ratings during purchase and social-risk tasks. This is a social/moral decision-making paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. The reported contrasts are within-task parametric associations (social risk modulation), not risk>safe, ambiguity contrasts, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is social/moral and not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no admissible risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrast). Full text is complete in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise maps (parametric modulations of reward and loss) and within-task contrasts (I5, I6, I7, I8 are met), the task is a value-based cost–benefit accept/reject paradigm without evidence of risky or ambiguous decision manipulations (no probabilities or uncertainty contrasts described). The review targets risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making; therefore the study is excluded under E5 (task not a qualifying risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4.

This is an fMRI study of a risky decision-making task (sequential box-opening with a ‘devil’), reporting within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Opt vs Nopt; GF vs MF; Nopt vs Devil). Group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses were performed with whole-brain inference and peak-level FWE thresholding; coordinate peaks are reported. Participants (n=18) are human and acceptable. Results are reported as tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during the Risky-Gains Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) in human adolescents (I4). Analyses are voxel-wise, whole-brain task-activation models with reported coordinates and peaks, and the model was fit over the whole brain (I6, I8). The reported analyses are within-group, voxel-wise correlations linking task-evoked activation (condition) to reductions in BMI and fat percentage, indicating a within-task decision-making contrast/modulation was tested (I5). Participant sample and ages are within acceptable ranges and the clinical group (excess weight) is allowed (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not PET, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are not solely task>implicit baseline in the documentation. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

E5 applies: the study investigates social decision-making (integration of social and individual information) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined for this review. While the study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts (satisfying I6) and reports coordinate peaks (satisfying I8), and the participant sample falls within allowed groups/ages (I7), it does not feature a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task (I4 not met) nor does it report accepted contrasts for risk/ambiguity/perceptual comparisons (I5 not met). Therefore it must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (satisfies I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with coordinate peaks (satisfies I6 and I8). Participant sample is acceptable (I7). However, the reported contrasts are 'last reversal error / final reversal errors' (simple within-group effects) and do not represent a decision-condition versus decision-condition contrast of the types required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). The extracted contrasts appear to be event-related error activations likely compared to implicit baseline, which meets exclusion criterion E3 (condition vs implicit baseline only). Therefore the study is excluded for failing to provide an eligible decision-making condition contrast (I5 not met) and for meeting E3.

This study reports fMRI of classical conditioning with odour detection and multivariate decoding/connectivity analyses, but it does not provide a within-group, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise contrast of a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparison of the admitted forms (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, risk>safe). Reported contrasts are session comparisons (post vs pre), ROI-restricted decoding, and seed-based connectivity with inference restricted to small volumes. Therefore it fails to meet required decision-making contrast and whole-brain task-evoked map criteria. Exclusion IDs: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast as defined for the meta-analysis) and E6 (results are ROI-restricted/no unmasked whole-brain task activation maps). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant groups acceptable) and I8 (reporting acceptable). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (does not test a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast as required), I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrasts), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map).

The study reports an fMRI experiment (BOLD) where participants performed modified Asian disease life-death decision problems with sure vs gamble options, i.e. a risky decision-making task (meets I4). Reported contrasts compare task conditions (e.g., positive/frame vs negative/frame contrasts P6 > N6 etc.), satisfying a condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast (meets I5). Analyses are group-level random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain models with peak coordinates reported in tables (meets I6 and I8). Participants are healthy humans within the acceptable age range (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not task>baseline only (not E3), not PET (not E4), not ROI-only (not E6), not connectivity-only (not E7), and include within-group contrasts (not E8). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the task is a probabilistic category/classification learning task with cognitive feedback, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrast matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and is excluded.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic value-learning (conditioning/reinforcement) task and reports contrasts such as correct>incorrect and rewarded>nonrewarded, not contrasts that index risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). While the paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses and reports coordinates (meeting I6, I7, I8), it does not meet I4 (task is not framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making per inclusion definitions) nor I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts). Therefore it is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM).

The study reports fMRI in human adolescents performing a Decision-Reward Uncertainty task that manipulates behavioral risk and reward risk. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (behavioral risk > no risk/reward risk; reward > no reward). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit and inference over whole brain; random-effects model; cluster-level FWE thresholding) with peaks reported in tables. Participants are healthy adolescents (n=31). Results are presented as coordinate peaks. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky/uncertain decision-making and provides whole-brain contrasts suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study used an fMRI risky decision-making task (I4) and reports results in tables/peaks (I8); participant sample is acceptable (I7). However, all reported analyses were region-of-interest (ROI) based (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I6 (requires whole-brain group-level maps) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). Additionally, the paper’s reported contrasts are primarily between-group comparisons and ROI correlations rather than unmasked whole-brain decision-condition contrasts. Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record only provides a whole-brain resting CBF between-group contrast (post-con > pre+con) and no whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI activation maps or decision-making contrasts. Although the abstract mentions a risky decision-making task and task-induced ventral striatum activation, the study document's extracted analyses include only a Rest Task (fixation) perfusion contrast (Analysis 28769072_analysis_0). Therefore the document lacks the required within-task, whole-brain group-level task activation contrast (I5, I6 not met). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (reports only resting/task-independent analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (only between-group contrasts reported with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task is reported in the abstract) and I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast documented) and I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map presented). Full text is complete as provided (no access problem).

The study reports fMRI during a probabilistic evidence-gathering decision task (Box Task) involving uncertainty, meeting the review focus. It includes within-subject contrasts that compare decision conditions (draw > conclusion and conclusion > draw) and an uncertainty contrast (60:40 > 80:20), matching the ambiguous/high-uncertainty contrast format. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; coordinate tables), and results are presented as peak coordinate tables. Participants are human healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study reports an fMRI task involving risky versus neutral decisions (risk scenarios from the Youth Risk Behavior Survey) with participants making choices and receiving outcomes (I4). It includes explicit condition-vs-condition contrasts comparing emotional outcomes tied to risky versus neutral decisions (e.g., Regret > Disappointment), which functionally reflect risky > neutral decision contrasts (I5). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests; model fit over whole brain) with peak coordinates provided (I6, I8). Participant ages (adolescents and young adults) fall within eligible ranges and any participant group is allowed (I7). No exclusion criteria appear to apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and within-group whole-brain task effects are present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusions.

The study reports fMRI during a reversal learning (decision-making under uncertainty) task (meets I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (meets I6) and participants include eligible groups (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (meets I8). However, the reported contrasts are parametric modulations of trialwise reward prediction error (PE) magnitudes and within-group PE associations, not condition-versus-condition decision-making contrasts of the types required (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 is not satisfied.

The task is a language-based preference choice between value words (managers vs non-managers) and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm, so it fails inclusion I4 and I5. The study does provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported as coordinates (I6 satisfied), uses healthy participants in an acceptable age range (I7 satisfied), and reports coordinates/tables (I8 satisfied). However, the reported contrasts are only between-group comparisons (managers > non-managers and the reverse) with no unmasked within-group task effect reported, so exclusion E8 also applies. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to investigate the target decision types (E5) and for reporting only between-group contrasts without within-group task effects (E8).

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is delay discounting / intertemporal choice, which is explicitly listed as excluded (E5). The study does meet inclusion criteria I5 (contains decision-making contrasts vs an active control: SS>control and LL>control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion I4 (task is risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is NOT met. No other exclusion criteria appear to apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making tasks.

The NeuroStore record reports event-related fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (meets I4), group-level whole-brain, random-effects GLM with reported peak coordinates (meets I6 and I8), and an eligible participant sample (meets I7). However, the reported contrasts are listed as 'anticipation [simple effect, within-group]' and 'experience [simple effect, within-group]' with no indication these are condition-versus-condition comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk) or task-versus-active-control contrasts required by I5. The label 'simple effect' strongly suggests these are task-period > implicit baseline contrasts rather than the allowed decision-condition comparisons. Therefore this study fails I5 and meets exclusion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline). Given this, it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (urn gambles with risky and ambiguous balls) and analyzes decision-related signals (belief updating, value updating, expectancy violation). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLMs were fit and inference was whole-brain with voxelwise correction (SnPM, whole-brain FWE). Contrasts are within-task parametric modulators reflecting decision processes (value/belief updating), which qualify as within-task comparisons for risky/ambiguous decision-making. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not PET, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are not only versus implicit baseline. Therefore the paper meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

Exclusion criteria met: E8 (the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts: all three analyses are group comparisons between autism and typically developing groups with no reported unmasked whole-brain within-group task effects). E5 (the task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm; the extracted contrasts are learning-phase and feedback-stage comparisons, not contrasts that map onto the review’s targeted risky-, ambiguous-, or perceptual-decision formats such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps were fit and inference was whole-brain), I7 (participant group is acceptable: clinical sample included), I8 (results reported as coordinate peaks, acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task does not clearly match the review’s specified classes of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), I5 (no contrast provided that matches the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons). Therefore exclude.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a decision-making task involving uncertainty (spatial prediction with changepoints and reward), with voxelwise, group-level whole-brain GLMs and permutation-based whole-brain FWE inference. Relevant contrasts include parametric modulations of changepoint probability (CPP) and relative uncertainty (RU), which correspond to ambiguity/uncertainty comparisons (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and thus meet the meta-analysis contrast requirements. Results are reported as whole-brain peaks (tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) (I4). It reports within-task decision-related contrasts/parametric modulations (e.g., Inflate*p(Explode) FU–BL, longitudinal changes in ‘Inflate’ decision signals) that qualify as decision-making contrasts (I5). Several group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps and inferences are reported (e.g., FU>BL, FU<BL, whole-brain correlations; model fit and inference over whole brain) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participant sample is acceptable (patients with substance dependence; inclusion allows clinical groups) (I7). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (reported peaks, tables) satisfying reporting allowance (I8). None of the exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical).

The study used fMRI during a reversal learning task and reports RPE parametric modulation and correlations with dopamine, but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Specifically, it lacks the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inference is restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (reported peaks from ROI), and no unmasked whole-brain task-activation results are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E5 (task not within risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and E6 (only ROI-reported results/no whole-brain results). Included criterion met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Not met: I4 (task type), I5 (required contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map).

This fMRI study primarily investigates social decision-making (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) and reports contrasts of unreciprocated vs reciprocated cooperation; these are social/outcome contrasts rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts. Although experiment 2 included a separate gamble task (small certain vs larger uncertain reward), the NeuroStore-extracted whole-brain contrasts reported are interaction and outcome contrasts ((CD-CC)–($0-$2), etc.) rather than a clear risky > safe or high-risk > low-risk main effect or a within-task risky-versus-safe choice contrast. Therefore the study does not provide a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast as required (I5 not met). It does, however, include fMRI during a gamble task (I4), reports whole-brain group results (I6), involves eligible participants (I7), and reports coordinates (I8). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper’s decision-making contrasts are social (Prisoner’s Dilemma) rather than the targeted risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM contrasts.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: (I4) It reports fMRI BOLD data collected while participants made risky investment decisions (choose between a bond and displayed investments with varied means and variances). (I5) It includes within-task contrasts/analyses relating neural activation to risk (reported correlation between risk of choice options and fMRI signal; GLM and DSFM-based contrasts of ID stimuli), which constitutes a decision-making contrast (high-risk vs low-risk / parametric risk effect). (I6) Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM (model fit over: whole brain; voxelwise GLM analysis reported). (I7) Participant group (n=19) is acceptable. (I8) Whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates (Table 5). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not PET, not baseline-only contrasts).

Study used task-based fMRI in humans performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task with parametric and condition contrasts indexing risk (e.g., associations between outcome-related activity and riskiness, linear decrease with riskiness, contrasts for negative/positive outcomes). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (analyses 0–3), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant sample (n=22 healthy adults) is acceptable. Although some pharmacological contrasts used ROI small-volume correction, the paper reports unmasked whole-brain task effects and coordinate peaks. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts with whole-brain results and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E8 met: the study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (Depression>Healthy, Healthy>Depression, group interactions including gain>loss) with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making gambling task), I5 (a decision-making condition contrast is reported — gain vs loss), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), I8 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: none of the inclusion criteria are wholly missing, but E8 mandates exclusion because only between-group contrasts are provided and no within-group whole-brain task effect is available in the document.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only inference/small-volume correction reported; inference restricted to region-of-interest), E8 (reported contrasts are between-group interactions with no clear unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear within-task decision condition contrast or task>control contrast reported in the document — available contrasts are between-group interactions), I6 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level voxelwise inference reported; inference was restricted to an ROI/SVC). Based on the provided NeuroStore record, the study does not provide the required whole-brain, unmasked task activation contrasts needed for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, so it should be excluded.

The task is a social communication/trust antecedent task (truth telling vs lying in a Sender/Receiver game) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The reported contrasts are true advice vs false advice and regression on risk-propensity score, not standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Whole-brain, group-level maps are reported, and participants are healthy. Therefore I6, I7, and I8 are met, but I4 and I5 are not met, and the study meets exclusion criterion E5 (social/moral decision-making rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM).

This study should be excluded because all reported fMRI analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) only (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task condition contrasts such as FC>NC and FF>NF), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain activation maps for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study used a probabilistic reversal learning/ reinforcement-learning task (Virtual Morris Water Maze variant) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Although the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (p<0.001 voxelwise) and within-group contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative feedback) and provides coordinates, the task and reported contrasts do not match the review’s required decision-making categories (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual). Therefore it does not meet the review’s task inclusion criteria.

The study used fMRI but the task was an oddball/vigilance listening task (catch-detection) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. The reported contrasts are multivariate decoding of interval quality (stimulus-category classification) not canonical perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence) nor a decision-task vs active control. Inference appears restricted to a region-of-interest despite searchlight model fitting, so no unmasked whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4, I5 and I6. It does meet I7 (participant sample acceptable) and I8 (reported peaks/coordinates). Exclusion criteria E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and E6 (only ROI-restricted results / no whole-brain results reported) apply.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic instrumental conditioning task (I4) and reports group-level whole-brain model estimates with reported peak coordinates (I6, I8). Participant sample is acceptable (I7). However, none of the reported contrasts correspond to a decision-making condition comparison required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy) or a decision-task > control-task contrast. The reported analyses are correlations with willingness-to-pay and feedback-evoked responses (initial vs later feedback correlations, parametric WTP modulation), not condition-versus-condition contrasts of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty; therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E9) are triggered. Because a required inclusion criterion (I5) is unmet, the study is excluded.

The study used fMRI during a card-guessing gambling task (risky decision-making) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. The GLM included a parametric regressor for cue-related uncertainty (i.e. high- vs low-uncertainty modulation), and the abstract and extracted analyses report activations for cue-related uncertainty and prediction error modulations across groups and within-group contrasts. Model fit and inference were whole-brain. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (contains a decision-making contrast via uncertainty parametric modulation/high vs low uncertainty), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (acceptable reporting format). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears available in the record provided.

This study used human fMRI (n=19) while participants performed a Multi-Armed Bandit decision-making task involving uncertainty (model entropy). It reports a whole-brain, group-level searchlight analysis with inference over the whole brain (cluster-based permutation testing) and includes within-task contrasts relating to entropy/uncertainty and exploit vs. explore behavior. These contrasts correspond to decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous/risky DM) and satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for condition-vs-condition or parametric uncertainty contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results of a probabilistic learning task and several parametric modulations (surprise, confidence, estimation update), but it does not present an explicit decision-making contrast of the required forms (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy) nor a task-vs-active-control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. The task is primarily a hierarchical probabilistic learning task rather than a clearly defined risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm (I4 not clearly met). The study does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported in tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Based on these points, I exclude the study.

This study used an fMRI mirror-reading/lexical decision task (mirror-reversed vs normal words). Although it reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (mirror > normal for runs 1–3) and provides coordinate tables, the task does not meet the review’s target decision-making domains. Specifically, the study examines reading/learning of mirror stimuli rather than risky, ambiguous, or prototypical perceptual decision-making manipulations (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (does not present an eligible decision-making contrast such as hard>easy or equivalent). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

The study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (controls > patients; condition-by-group interaction) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects provided. The task is an instrumental conditioning/reward-learning paradigm contrasting gain vs loss and prediction-error signals, but it does not present a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation of the types specified (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Thus it fails inclusion I4 and I5. It does meet whole-brain group-level reporting (I6), participant eligibility (I7), and acceptable reporting format (I8). Exclusion criteria E8 (only between-group contrasts reported) and E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making (tactile discrimination) task with subsequent confidence ratings. NeuroStore lists a group-level, whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) parametric modulation analysis associating BOLD with decisional confidence (GLM, one-sample t-test; reported peak coordinates, FWE cluster-level thresholding). These features satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion requirements: an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), a task-related within-task contrast (parametric modulation of a decision-related variable—confidence) that constitutes a condition-wise task effect (I5), whole-brain group-level evidence (I6), allowable participant sample (I7), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not between-group-only). Therefore the study should be included.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (Analysis 15689962_analysis_0). However, the task is reversal learning and the reported contrasts concern treatment (acute tryptophan depletion) effects and reversal-switch errors versus correct responses, not contrasts of risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or perceptual difficulty contrasts required by the review. Therefore it does not meet the review’s decision-making domain criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (reporting format acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM). Decision: EXCLUDED.

Exclusion applied: E5. This study used an fMRI two-step revaluation/reinforcement-learning/planning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as required. Included criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast of the admitted forms such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy; analyses are parametric modulations and rest contrasts predicting replay/replanning rather than condition-vs-condition decision contrasts). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used an emotion-recognition (face Stroop) task manipulating emotional-congruency (incongruent vs congruent) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or canonical perceptual decision-making manipulation (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Although it reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (coordinate tables) for condition-vs-condition comparisons, the task does not constitute risky, ambiguous, or the types of perceptual decision-making targeted by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails the core inclusion requirement for task domain and is excluded.

This study reports fMRI during a risky decision-making task (gamble choices varying in probability and magnitude) and provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. Multiple reported analyses are within-group parametric contrasts (e.g. context-dependent desirability, magnitude vs probability weighting) and a between-subjects regression using an intransitivity index; models were fit over the whole brain and inference was performed voxelwise with reported peak coordinates. These analyses constitute within-task, condition-related contrasts (parametric modulations) appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of risky decision-making. Participants are healthy adults and results are clearly reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts/parametric modulations), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates neural responses to observing shared vs parallel intentions (social cognition) and contrasts an Intention task vs a Color (dot-monitoring) task. The meta-analysis requires fMRI of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Although the paper reports group-level, whole-brain activation maps (coordinates, Monte Carlo thresholding) and acceptable participant sample, its tasks are social/intentional perception rather than risky, ambiguous, or defined perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Therefore it does not meet I4 (task type) nor I5 (required decision-making contrasts). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results clearly reported). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) applies, so the study is excluded.

The study reports fMRI during a decision-making task manipulating subjective uncertainty (I4 satisfied) and includes whole-brain group-level analyses (analyses 22461182_analysis_2 and _3 indicate model fit and inference over whole brain) (I6 satisfied). Participant samples are acceptable (I7) and reporting of whole-brain results in tables/peaks is present (I8). However, all extracted contrasts are between-group comparisons (OCD patients > controls) for specific task conditions; there is no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or within-task contrast (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty) reported in the NeuroStore record. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (requirement for an appropriate within-task or task-vs-control contrast) is not met. Based on E8, the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the task (Serial Reaction Time Task) is a sequence learning/motor task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reported whole-brain group-level statistical maps/analyses present), I7 (participant group acceptable; healthy adults), I8 (results reported with coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a qualifying risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task is not satisfied), I5 (no contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or task versus active control; reported analyses are parametric modulations of learning signals rather than condition contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study used passive visual viewing (participants were instructed not to try to solve the problems), so it did not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (fails I4). No contrast compares decision-making conditions or a decision task against an active control task (fails I5). It does report a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level regression with reported peak coordinates (meets I6), includes eligible participants (meets I7), and reports whole-brain results in tables (meets I8). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the reported task/contrast is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment (BOLD) in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between a sure thing and gambles with varying probabilities). It includes within-group contrasts comparing decision conditions (high probability > low probability) and high-value > low-value, satisfying condition-vs-condition comparisons. The statistical model was fit and inference reported across the whole brain (voxelwise), with coordinates/tables of peaks provided. Results are presented in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

The Ultimatum Game is a social/fairness decision-making task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion E5 applies. The study does meet several inclusion criteria (I5: within-task condition contrasts such as fair vs selfish and high vs low stakes; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peaks; I7: eligible participant group; I8: whole-brain results reported in tables), but it fails I4 (the task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual). No other exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

The study includes a Risky Decision-Making Task (probabilities 20–60%) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (analyses 1 and 2) reporting peaks for parametric modulation by relative subjective value. This satisfies I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation of decision-related value qualifies as condition-wise contrasts), I6 (model fit and inference reported over the whole brain), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates). Although the paper also contains delay-discounting (intertemporal) analyses, that does not violate inclusion because at least one qualifying risky-DM contrast is present.
