No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E9) apply: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group whole-brain task effects rather than only task>rest or between-group-only contrasts. Thus the record should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI BOLD experiment in humans (n=21) using a gambling/card-guessing task that manipulates risk (gamble vs certain option) and contextual reward distributions. It contains explicit within-group, group-level second-level GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peaks in MNI space. Crucially, contrasts match the meta-analysis’ risky-DM contrasts (e.g., risky > non-risky choices; gambling choices > certain option choices). Although inference was sometimes restricted via small-volume correction (SVC) in regions of interest, the GLMs were estimated voxelwise across the whole brain (satisfying whole-brain, group-level mapping). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not connectivity-only, not task-vs-baseline only). Therefore the article meets the review’s inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI whole-brain contrasts and is included.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (categorization of auditory and tactile sweeps) performed in humans (n=21). The study reports within-task contrasts of decision conditions (cross-decoding between learned category/direction conditions) rather than contrasts against baseline. Group-level, whole-brain (searchlight) voxelwise statistical maps were tested (group-level t tests of cross-decoding accuracies with permutation TFCE FWE correction and inference over the whole brain), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults within allowable age range. Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (Table 1). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because its task and contrasts do not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (Exclusion E5). The reported task is an Old/New recognition memory task using facial attractiveness stimuli, and contrasts compare attractive versus less attractive faces rather than any risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty conditions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable; healthy adults), I8 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no contrast compares decision-making conditions such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No other exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This fMRI study used a gambling (risky) task and reports group-level, whole-brain parametric maps (satisfying I4, I6). Participants are healthy and reporting is acceptable (I7, I8). However, all reported contrasts are parametric modulators (RP, RPE, LP, LPE) tested as associations (e.g., RP > 0) rather than condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts of the forms specified in I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, task > control). The manuscript does not present contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions or an active control, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

The study used fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task manipulating reward probability (HP vs LP), i.e., decision-making under uncertainty. It reports within-subject, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., HP>LP, reversal errors > all positive) and associations (prediction error correlations), estimated over the whole brain and reported voxelwise peaks. These satisfy the review’s requirements for an fMRI decision-making task, condition-vs-condition contrasts, and whole-brain group-level maps. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only baseline contrasts, ROI-only, PET, resting-state, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports an fMRI reversal learning task but provides only ROI-based task activation (SVC) and seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results and omnibus between-group contrasts. There is no unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map or within-group task contrasts of the kinds required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results), E7 (reports only seed-based connectivity/gPPI without whole-brain task activation map), E8 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reversal-learning task—not clearly one of the predefined risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks as required), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which participants made perceptual classifications of ambiguous auditory stimuli (word vs pseudoword), i.e. a perceptual decision-making task. The abstract explicitly states they contrasted word-versus-pseudoword trials, and NeuroStore lists within-group simple effects for word-perceived and pseudoword-perceived and judgment conditions, indicating decision-related condition contrasts. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates and FDR correction (p<0.05), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Subjects were healthy adults. Therefore the study meets the review’s fMRI perceptual decision-making objective and provides qualifying whole-brain contrasts and coordinate results. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/ connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports whole-brain fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task and reports contrasts involving high-risk vs low-risk choices, but the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction contrasts (pathological gamblers vs controls) and no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effects (e.g., risky>safe within a group). This meets exclusion E8 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text is available from the NeuroStore record (not incomplete). Therefore the study must be excluded per E8.

The Paper-Scissors-Rock task is a reinforcement-learning/conditioning task and is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm (violates I4). The NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (abstinent > relapsed, relapsed > abstinent, early/late trials between groups) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy), so it meets exclusion E8. It does report whole-brain group-level maps and coordinate tables, and participant groups are acceptable.

The study used the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task and reports a contrast of Loss Cue > Neutral Cue (Nicotine vs Placebo interaction). Although it provides whole-brain, group-level fMRI results (coordinates/peaks) and includes an eligible participant group, the MID is a reward-anticipation task without an uncertainty/risk or perceptual difficulty manipulation, and the reported contrast is not a decision-making contrast of the forms required (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it does not meet inclusion I4 (risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) nor I5 (required decision-making contrast). It does meet I6 (whole-brain evidence), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported as peaks). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) applies. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a lottery task that manipulated outcome uncertainty (OU) and expected value (EV). Reported, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses include parametric modulation of OU (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty contrasts) and contrasts at curiosity relief; results are reported as peak coordinates with whole-brain inference. These features satisfy inclusion: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous-like task manipulating uncertainty), I5 (contrasts/parametric modulation reflecting uncertainty effects), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not baseline-only). Although participants could not influence outcomes and primarily rated curiosity, the core manipulation and reported whole-brain uncertainty contrasts meet the review’s decision-making uncertainty criteria.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a visual search (contextual cueing) task that manipulates target-location predictability (50% vs 100% vs unpredicted), which constitutes an uncertainty/ambiguity manipulation relevant to ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). The reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (mixed-effects FLAME I; model fit over whole brain; MNI coordinates; reported peaks) provides a within-task contrast (CoTv > CoTf) comparing decision-making conditions rather than task>baseline. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activation peaks (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the reported within-group contrast is task > rest (task versus implicit baseline) and no condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast is provided; this violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against rest). Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in table). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying condition-vs-condition or task vs active control contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only task > rest contrasts).

Excluded per E8: The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction/contrast (group-by-condition) comparing probabilistic versus fixed choices across IGD and HC, with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (e.g., risky > safe) reported. The study otherwise satisfies inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky/probability decision-making task), I5 (contrast comparing probabilistic vs fixed choices), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (allowed participant groups), and I8 (peaks/coordinates reported). Because the only reported whole-brain result is a between-group contrast/interaction and no within-group task activation map is provided, it must be excluded according to E8.

The study used a reversal-learning decision task (monetary feedback) so I4 (task is a decision-making paradigm) is satisfied, and participant inclusion fits allowable groups so I7 is satisfied. However all reported analyses were ROI-based (model fit and inference restricted to anatomical ROIs) with no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps, violating I6 and meeting exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses). Additionally, the reported contrasts are presented as between-group interactions (patient vs. control contrasts) with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effects, meeting exclusion E8. Because I6 and I5 (no qualifying within-task decision contrasts reported as required) are not satisfied and E6/E8 apply, the study must be excluded.

The study uses an fMRI social-perception learning task (predicting targets' agree/disagree responses) and reports contrasts like incorrect>correct and yea-sayer>naysayer, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision contrasts. This makes it a social decision-making paradigm, which falls under exclusion E5. The paper does provide group-level whole-brain maps (Model fit over: whole brain) and reports coordinates/tables, and participants fall within allowable groups/ages. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain evidence), I7 (acceptable participant groups), I8 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no qualifying contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is social, not one of the targeted DM types). Full text was sufficiently represented in the provided document.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (dot numerosity estimation) (I4). The reported contrast is a within-task comparison of decision conditions (Conformity to In-group > Non-Conformity to In-group), which is an acceptable within-task decision-making contrast (I5). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM with model fit over the whole brain and reported MNI peak coordinates (I6, I8). Participant sample (n=24 healthy adults) is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, and not connectivity-only. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The task is a probabilistic reinforcement learning/pair-associates learning task with reward/punishment outcomes and prediction-error analyses, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm. Included criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant sample acceptable), I8 (results reported as peak coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual hard>easy). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual), E8 (the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked within-group task effect reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study used fMRI during a gambling/probabilistic reward task in Parkinson’s patients (risky decision-making domain) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (satisfies I4, I6, I7, I8). However, NeuroStore’s extraction shows the reported contrasts are medication comparisons (DA > OFF/LD, OFF > LD/DA, LD > DA), outcome-related effects, and parametric correlations with reward prediction error or risk-taking scores. The record does not report any decision-making contrast that matches the required forms for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, hard > easy, or task > control). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or task vs active control in the accepted forms) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are otherwise triggered by the available record.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment of perceptual category learning (visual classification of distorted dot patterns), satisfying I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task). The reported contrast (untrained > trained) is a within-task, between-condition decision-making contrast, meeting I5. The analysis was performed and inferred over the whole brain at the group level with voxelwise FDR correction and reported peak coordinates, meeting I6 and I8. Participants are human and healthy (n=27), acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria are violated: this is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not resting-state/connectivity-only (E7), and the reported contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline (not E3). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions apply.

Excluded because the paper reports ROI-restricted voxelwise path analyses of white-matter (model fit and inference restricted to NAcc-connected pathways) rather than a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI activation map. The manuscript does include an fMRI risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports NAcc activation (I4) and the participant sample is eligible (I7). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any within-task contrast maps (e.g., risky>safe) or a whole-brain, voxelwise group activation map: model fit over and inference restricted to a region of interest (probabilistic tractography masks) indicates results are ROI-only. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met; inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied (no explicit decision-condition contrast reported and no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text is complete enough for screening.

This fMRI study used a lottery decision-making task manipulating prior and likelihood information about reward probability (risky/uncertain decision-making). Reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (third-level mixed-effects) with whole-brain inference and familywise error correction. The reported contrasts are within-group parametric modulations (associations) with decision-related variables (mean of posterior distribution; mean of prior distribution), which qualify as within-task decision-making contrasts rather than simple task>baseline contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply: not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making and should be included.

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group parametric contrasts/ interactions (e.g., model-based RPE and learning-rate modulations reported as between-group effects) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrast or condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast. Exclusion ID met: E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement-learning decision task involving uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results reported in standard whole-brain format). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (no contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or decision task vs an active control task of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Because E8 is met (only between-group contrasts reported), the study must be excluded.

The study reports fMRI in humans (n=32) performing a sequential inference task involving uncertainty about a hidden variable (occluded helicopter), which fits ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I4). It includes within-group parametric contrasts reflecting uncertainty-related variables (e.g., Uncertainty, Change Point Probability, shifting latent state), satisfying the requirement for decision-related contrasts such as high- vs low-uncertainty type effects (I5). Multiple analyses were conducted as whole-brain searchlight group-level analyses with voxelwise inference using cluster-based permutation testing and reported peak coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6) and acceptable reporting (I8). Participant sample is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not against implicit baseline only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and are empirical. Therefore the article should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study recorded BOLD while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (Gabor detection with confidence judgments), satisfying I4. It reports within-task condition contrasts (unexpected vs expected Gabor presence/absence; congruent vs incongruent confidence interactions), which are condition-versus-condition decision-making contrasts meeting I5. Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLMs and report whole-brain inference (Analysis 0: stimulus-sensitive area), satisfying I6. Participant sample and reporting meet I7 and results are clearly described, meeting I8. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not only connectivity without task activation (E7) because a whole-brain task activation contrast is reported, and contrasts are not against implicit baseline only (E3). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast as required by I5. The paper reports an encoding-model association (EEG-informed fMRI) during a perceptual decision task and provides a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise map (analysis 0). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported in standard forms). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or task vs active control such as hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I5.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (choices between high-risk and low-risk options) with BOLD measures (I4). It includes contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (high-risk > low-risk), matching the risky-DM contrast formats (I5). Analyses were fitted over the whole brain and reported group-level, random-effects, voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates (I6 and I8). Participant characteristics are within acceptable ranges and any group qualifies (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record shows fMRI during the Probabilistic Classification Learning Task (PCLT) with an active perceptual-matching control (PMCT), whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and coordinate reporting. However, the only reported statistical contrasts are interaction/between-group contrasts (PCLT vs PMCT interaction between healthy comparison and psychosis-risk groups). No unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (e.g., PCLT > PMCT within a group) is reported; thus the study meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions without within-group task effects). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with responses given after stimulus, satisfying I4. The paper reports parametric contrasts with motion coherence (positive and negative parametric effects), which constitute within-task condition comparisons equivalent to 'low coherence > high coherence' style contrasts, satisfying I5. Two analyses (22922368_analysis_2 and _3) are group-level whole-brain GLM tests with reported peak coordinates, meeting I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults (n=22), satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not against implicit baseline only (E3), this is fMRI not PET (E4), task is perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only, E6), and this is an empirical within-group task activation study (not E7/E8/E9). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making (gain/loss framing) task in 143 human participants. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (frame-consistent vs frame-inconsistent choices; contrasts reflect safe vs gamble choices across frames), which are decision-making condition comparisons qualifying under the risky-DM examples. Analyses were fit and tested voxelwise across the whole brain with TFCE FWE correction, and reported peaks are provided. Participants are an acceptable healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This fMRI study reports human perceptual decision-making (delayed match-to-sample with auditory and tactile sweep directions) and includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (up-sweeps > down-sweeps). Analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain inference (univariate whole-brain GLM and searchlight multivariate whole-brain inference) and corrected cluster-level FWER; results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=40). Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition decision contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline, and it is empirical). Full text is available in the provided record.

This study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts such as Endpoints vs Boundaries and 40% vs 50%), and I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults). However, all reported statistical inferences were restricted to predefined regions-of-interest using small-volume correction (inference restricted to ROI; thresholding via 3dClustSim SVC). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps are reported. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Because I6 is not satisfied and E6 is met, the study is excluded.

This study meets the review scope and inclusion criteria. It acquired fMRI during a decision-making (instrumental causal learning) task involving choices described as selecting more/less risky options (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts (parametric modulators of learning/confidence parameters and outcome-related modulators) that constitute condition-wise, within-task comparisons relevant to risk/uncertainty (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (whole-brain one-sample t-tests; coordinates/tables provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting formats (I8). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable per I7. Although one between-session (placebo>ketamine) contrast was ROI-restricted, multiple whole-brain within-group task effects are available, so exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) are not met. Therefore include.

Excluded because the task and reported contrasts do not match the meta-analysis’ decision-making contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the Instrumental Conditioning/probabilistic feedback learning task is a feedback-learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review) and E8 (the reported analyses are labelled as between-group contrasts/interactions with no unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect reported). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making tasks) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is social decision-making (game of Chicken) rather than a non-social risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as required. While the study reports whole-brain fMRI results (I6), includes an eligible participant sample (I7), and reports coordinates/peaks (I8), it does not present an eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast meeting I5 (the only extracted contrast is human > computer, and the risky > safe comparison is not provided in the available record). Therefore I4/I5 are not met and E5 excludes the study from the meta-analysis. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used fMRI during an uncertainty/anticipation task (meets I4) and includes a contrast of uncertain > certain anticipation consistent with ambiguous decision-making (meets I5). Participants are healthy young adults (meets I7). However, all reported analyses were region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs with small-volume correction) and no unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps are reported. This violates the whole-brain requirement (I6) and therefore meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). The paper also reports only between-group interaction contrasts (amber/placebo vs blue light) with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect, meeting exclusion E8. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI)-based analyses with inference restricted to anatomical ROIs (model fit and inference over ROI only), and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual/probabilistic classification decision-making task), I5 (task > active perceptual-motor baseline contrast present), and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results). Therefore the study cannot be included in the whole-brain activation meta-analysis.

Excluded because the task is social cooperation (Prisoner’s Dilemma vs Stag Hunt) and therefore does not target risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map reported), I7 (participants are healthy adults, an acceptable group), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task not satisfied), I5 (contrast does not match allowed risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts; PD>SH is social cooperation comparison). Fulltext is complete for screening.

Exclusion(s) met: E5, E7, E8. The task is a reward-learning/monetary guessing task without a clear risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation (violates I4/I5). Reported contrasts are cross-subject regressions with trauma and seed-based gPPI connectivity (and an ROI activation analysis) rather than within-task decision-condition contrasts or an unmasked whole-brain task activation map (violates I5 and I6; meets E7 and E8). Inclusion(s) met: I7 (human participants of relevant ages/clinical status). Inclusion(s) not met: I4 (task not clearly risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no decision-condition contrasts such as risky>safe or hard>easy), I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This study used an altruistic/social decision-making task (deciding whether to transfer points to a partner) with manipulations labeled “self-risk” and “other-need,” but the decision context is social/altruistic rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. This falls under exclusion E5 (social decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant sample acceptable), I8 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5 (the task does not constitute a standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; contrasts are parametric social-modulator associations rather than the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). No other exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is excluded per E5.

Excluded because the study does not report a task-based, whole-brain fMRI contrast of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task; the reported task is Rest), I5 (no decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast is reported), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the paper is not eligible for the meta-analysis of task-evoked decision-making fMRI studies.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (coordinates/tables) in healthy participants and thus meets criteria I6, I7 and I8. However, the task is social/moral decision-making (financially helping versus harming others) and the reported contrasts are about valence, magnitude, intention, and choice (self vs charity). There are no contrasts matching risky (>safe, high-risk>low-risk), ambiguous (>low uncertainty), or perceptual (hard>easy, low coherence>high) decision-making as required. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) and fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a perceptual decision-making (visual masking) task with within-task condition contrasts (e.g., short stimulus/mask timing vs long timing) that correspond to perceptual difficulty (hard > easy). Group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain model fit and inference; peak coordinates and a table are provided). Participants are healthy adults (n=27) within the eligible age range. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts, whole-brain group maps, and reporting of results. No exclusion criteria apply.

While the study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (predicting which ball reaches first) and includes at least one whole-brain group-level analysis, it does not report any contrast that compares decision-making conditions of interest for this meta-analysis (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, or a decision-task > control-task). The reported contrasts focus on feedback valence and agency (self- vs external-attributed gains/losses) rather than perceptual decision difficulty or decision-versus-control contrasts required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore I4 and I6 are met, but I5 is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (I4) with within-task contrasts (e.g., correct vs incorrect/misperception; I5) in a healthy participant sample (I7). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based with model fitting and thresholding restricted to ROIs rather than a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and corresponds to exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). No whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps are reported, so the study must be excluded.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI study of a risky decision task (BART) with a reported whole-brain, group-level omnibus between-group contrast (gender-by-stress interaction) and peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical map reported), I7 (healthy participants qualify), and I8 (results reported as coordinate table). However, the record lists only a between-group omnibus contrast and does not report any unmasked whole-brain within-group task contrasts or task-vs-control contrasts required to index decision vs decision/control conditions. Therefore exclusion E8 applies (only between-group contrasts reported with no accompanying within-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (a within-task or task>control decision-making contrast) is not met.

This fMRI study measured BOLD while participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion direction discrimination) and reports a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise parametric modulation of neural activity by an EEG-derived confidence signal (third-level mixed-effects FLAME 1). The analysis is a within-task decision-related contrast (trial-by-trial confidence modulation), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast. Whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates are provided. Participants are healthy humans. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (within-task decision-related contrast via parametric modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not PET, not connectivity-only (there is also a task activation map), and contrasts are not only task>rest. Thus include.

This study used a Trust Game (social dilemma) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm and therefore does not meet the review’s domain inclusion (I4). Although it reports decision-task-versus-control contrasts (I5), whole-brain group-level maps (I6), appropriate participant groups (I7), and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I8), the core task is social/moral decision-making rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM, so exclusion criteria apply. Additionally, the paper reports primarily between-group (high-Mach vs low-Mach) whole-brain contrasts and lacks an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (only region-of-interest within-group analyses are present), meeting E8 as well. Therefore exclude (E5, E8).

The study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion RDM) with explicit task and active control conditions (task vs control coherence), meeting the definition of perceptual DM. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain, GLM mixed-effects, voxel-level FDR thresholding) and provides reported peak coordinates. Contrasts include task > control and parametric modulation contrasts, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and matched healthy controls) are acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only task>rest contrasts, and includes within-task task>control effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The task is a reversal-learning task (feedback-based stimulus–response reversal), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. The reported contrasts (e.g., last reversal error > baseline; between-group interactions) do not match required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms (I5). Whole-brain, group-level activation maps and coordinate peaks are reported, and participants are an acceptable sample, but the core decision-making domain criterion is not met. Inclusion met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion not met: I4, I5. Exclusion applied: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task).

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making (2AFC heading) task (I4). It reports within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (EASY > HARD; COH EASY > HARD), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast (I5). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM with reported peak coordinates (model fit over whole brain; thresholding and reported peaks), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting in tables of coordinates (I8). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition vs condition (not task>baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the task is a perceptual decision task. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria; include in meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a guessing task manipulating uncertainty (guessing colour vs suit) and reports contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (guessing > reporting; higher-uncertainty suit > lower-uncertainty colour). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results with corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates. The task clearly involves decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous decision-making), meeting the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts).

This fMRI study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task manipulating outcome probability and magnitude (e.g., 80% > 20%, $5.00 > $0.00), producing condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps were fit and inference was reported across the whole brain (coordinate peaks and FDR-thresholded results are listed). Participants were healthy humans (n=14). The reported contrasts (probability, magnitude, EV, valence) satisfy the review’s risky-DM contrast forms (e.g., high-risk/high-probability > low-risk/low-probability). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, not baseline-only contrasts, and it is empirical fMRI task data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making whole-brain fMRI and should be included.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI perceptual decision-making task with contrasts comparing face versus house decisions (meets I4 and I5). However, all reported analyses in the document are seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results (Result: connectivity; Model: PPI with nucleus accumbens seed). There is no evidence in this document of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (contrast map) for the decision task. According to the review criteria, studies that report only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses without also reporting whole-brain task activation maps must be excluded (E7). Therefore the study is excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported in this document). Exclusion criteria applied: E7.

The study reports a whole-brain, group-level interaction contrast comparing emotional face conditions with an oval control across groups (HCL FEAR/HAPPY/SAD > MDD OVAL). While it involves an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), includes a task-vs-control contrast form (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I6) with acceptable participant samples (I7) and reporting format (I8), the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts/interactions and does not provide any unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI delayed match-to-sample task where participants made perceptual recognition decisions (probe trials) about color matches versus no-probe (no-decision) trials and manipulated sample-probe similarity (matching difficulty). It therefore addresses perceptual decision-making. NeuroStore shows group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with FDR voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (satisfies whole-brain evidence). Relevant contrasts include probe vs no-probe (decision task versus active control) and manipulations of matching difficulty and load, meeting the requirement for at least one decision-making condition comparison. Participants (n=21) are human and healthy. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not versus implicit baseline only, not PET, not ROI-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) experiment in human participants performing a modified beads task (probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making). It includes at least one within-group, task-versus-control contrast (JTC > control) reported as a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects analysis with thresholded peaks (voxelwise FWE p<0.05), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Whole-brain results are reported in tables of peaks. Therefore the paper meets I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (task > control contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain map), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports a task in which participants performed perceptual identification (images gradually revealed from noise) while undergoing fMRI and makes trialwise uncertainty/entropy manipulations. The NeuroStore record shows multiple whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level non-parametric methods; MNI coordinates reported) that test uncertainty-related contrasts/parametric effects (e.g., higher-state-level entropy, structure-level entropy, ‘uncertainty < low uncertainty’, parametric correlations with surprise/entropy). Thus it meets: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual/uncertainty decision task), I5 (within-task uncertainty/entropy contrasts/parametric tests comparable to “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, contrasts are condition-vs-condition or parametric uncertainty effects rather than implicit baseline).

This study reports an fMRI experiment with human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion), and reports within-group omnibus contrasts for motion coherence and stimulus duration. The NeuroStore record indicates a group-level, whole-brain model fit and reports peak coordinates (tables), with task-related regressors (motion coherence; duration) and component-level inference identifying regions sensitive to coherence (i.e., perceptual difficulty) — satisfying the required contrast type (perceptual: low coherence vs high coherence / main effect of coherence). All inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not task>rest only (E3), not PET (E4), task is perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (not only ROI; E6), and although ICA was used, task-evoked component effects and whole-brain peaks are reported (so E7 does not apply). The NeuroStore record appears complete for screening. Note: sample size is small (n=5) but this does not violate inclusion rules.

The study used fMRI during a Card-Guessing (Gambling) task (risky decision-making) and reports task contrasts that manipulate risk level (group × risk choice interactions and contrasts referencing low- vs high-risk outcomes). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level SPM models were fit and inference was whole-brain FWE-corrected at the voxel level, and peak coordinates are reported. Participants fall within allowable samples. Thus the paper provides whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts that compare decision-making conditions (risk levels), satisfying the review’s focus on risky decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, task vs baseline only, connectivity-only, or solely between-group contrasts without any within-group contrast) are met. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study used event-related fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic classification learning task that manipulated stimulus-outcome contingency (deterministic vs probabilistic), i.e., an uncertainty/ambiguity decision-making manipulation. The reported contrast Det-CP > Prob-CP directly compares two decision-making conditions (deterministic vs probabilistic). The model was fit over the whole brain with a group-level, random-effects GLM and voxelwise inference (p<0.005) with reported peak coordinates. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (contrast comparing decision conditions), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise results). Participants are healthy (I7) and whole-brain results are reported (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only). Full text is available in the record provided.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (phoneme identification) and reports contrasts comparing phoneme identification (/r/ + /l/) to vowels, so it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (perceptual task > control-type contrast), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results described). However, all reported analyses indicate the model was fit and inference was restricted to region(s) of interest (ROIs) rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Because I6 is required, the study must be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (near-threshold pain detection where participants judged stimuli as painful vs non-painful). It includes within-subject contrasts of decision conditions (pain > no pain) and an interaction with threat (high > low), which constitute condition-versus-condition decision-making contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholds; reported peak coordinates in MNI). Participants are healthy humans (n=16). The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and not baseline-only contrasts). Full text is available in the record provided.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual categorization task (probabilistic, evidence-accumulation) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps (parametric modulators of categorical evidence and confidence, and urgency interactions). These contrasts are within-task decision-making effects (decision variables comparable to perceptual difficulty/evidence contrasts) and are reported at whole-brain, voxelwise inference thresholds (tables of peaks provided). ROI analyses are present but do not exclude the study because several qualifying whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply.

This study is excluded. Exclusion reasons: E5 (task is delay discounting / intertemporal choice, which the review excludes) and E6 (analyses are region-of-interest only; model fit and inference restricted to ventral/dorsal striatum with no whole-brain voxelwise group map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (there is a within-task decision contrast LL>SS), I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy adolescents), I8 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion E5 (task not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E6 (only ROI-inference reported with small-volume correction; no unmasked whole-brain results) apply. The study used a probabilistic reversal learning task and reports correlational/parametric analyses of prediction-error BOLD and cross-subject regressions (fluid IQ, SLES) rather than contrasts of decision conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Included criteria met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of the target decision-making categories), I5 (no qualifying decision-condition contrasts), and effectively I6 (no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked results reported; inference restricted to ROI). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports only resting-state fMRI and seed-based functional connectivity analyses (RSC and TOS seeds) with no task-based decision-making contrasts or task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (only seed-based/resting-state analyses with no whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task; task is rest), I5 (no decision-making contrast or task versus active control), I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study used Ultimatum/Dictator Game contrasts (unfair > fair, etc.), which are social/fairness decisions rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Therefore it does not meet I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) nor I5 (contains one of the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). It does report whole-brain, group-level activation maps (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and reports coordinates/peaks in tables (I8). Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study reports a whole-brain, group-level contrast (negative > positive surprise) from an emotional face perception task; however the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion E5 applies because the decision-making task is not one of the target types (this is an emotion/valence task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map reported), I7 (human participants; eligible group), I8 (results reported with coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), I5 (contrast comparing decision-making conditions or decision-making vs control). Therefore the study is excluded.

This concurrent TMS-fMRI study collected BOLD data while participants performed a perceptual detection task (visual signal detection), satisfying I4. It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision outcomes (misses > hits; misses > correct rejections), which are acceptable within-task perceptual decision-making contrasts per I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (model fit over whole brain; permutation-based FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy humans and thus meet I7. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not implicit baseline) so E3 is not met; this is fMRI (not PET) so E4 is not met; the task is perceptual decision-making (not an excluded task) so E5 is not met; whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only) so E6 is not met; connectivity-only analyses are not the sole report so E7 is not met; within-group contrasts are present so E8 is not met; and the study is empirical (not a review) so E9 is not met.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual decision task (I4 met) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise component maps (group ICA components tested with one-sample t tests; I6 met). Participant sample is acceptable (I7 met) and results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I8 met). However, the paper does not report any condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts of decision-making (e.g., hard>easy, perceptual task>control); instead it reports ICA component simple-effects (one-sample tests on component loadings), which do not constitute the required decision-making contrasts. Therefore it lacks the required decision-making contrasts (I5 not met) and effectively provides only task/component effects likely vs implicit baseline, triggering exclusion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/rest/fixation). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E3. Full text appears complete for abstraction (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI. It used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) during fMRI (I4), and reports within-task parametric contrasts modulated by probability of explosion (inflation choice×P(explode); successful inflation×P(explode)), which are condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts (I5). Analyses were estimated and inferred over the whole brain with group-level random-effects GLMs and reported peak coordinates (I6, I8). Participant sample (including alcohol-dependent individuals) is acceptable per criteria (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not only task>baseline (E3), this is not PET (E4), the task is a risky DM task (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only, E6), and it is task-activation GLM (not only connectivity or resting, E7). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (synchronous vs asynchronous audiovisual judgments) in human participants (n=33), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (asynchrony > synchrony and related contrasts), satisfying I5. The NeuroStore record reports group-level activation peaks in MNI coordinates (Table 1) for the task contrasts, which counts as whole-brain results reported as coordinates (I6 and I8). Participants and sample type are acceptable (I7). Although one analysis was described as ROI-based (Thalamus), other reported peaks and coordinate space indicate voxelwise group results across the brain, and the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity analyses in addition to task activations; thus it does not meet exclusion criteria E6 or E7. Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the paper does not report an eligible decision-making contrast as required by I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual categorization task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task contrasts reported for feedback contrasts), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no contrast matching the required perceptual-DM forms such as hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or task>control; reported contrasts are decoding accuracy and feedback-based contrasts like positive>negative and incorrect>correct, which are not the specified perceptual decision difficulty or task-vs-control comparisons). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Therefore exclude for failure to meet I5.

Exclusion: The study does not present any contrast matching the meta-analysis’ required decision-making comparisons (I5). While it is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level maps during a speeded perceptual/motor task, the reported contrasts focus on temporal predictability (good vs bad clock), accessory-stimulus arousal (accessory vs no accessory), and hand-specific motor activity, plus task>rest contrasts. None correspond to the admissible perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence) nor to the specified risky- or ambiguity-DM contrasts (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Therefore I5 is not satisfied and the study is excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual/speeded task), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), I8 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

The study used an fMRI reversal-learning/probabilistic reinforcement-learning task (meets I4) and reports results and tables (meets I8); participant groups are eligible (meets I7). However, the task is a reinforcement-learning paradigm rather than a clearly defined risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as required (violates I5 / matches exclusion E5). Critically, the reported task-evoked fMRI effects rely on parametric prediction-error regressors with inference restricted to small-volume/ROI analyses (even where the model was fit over the whole brain), and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported (violates I6 and matches exclusion E6). Therefore the paper should be excluded from the meta-analysis. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6. Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6.

The task is a statistical learning/conditioning paradigm (predicting symbol sequences) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Although the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample maps (satisfying I6) and reports coordinates/peaks (I8) with an eligible participant sample (I7), it does not present any contrasts of the forms required for this meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task). Full text is available in the provided record.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an animal-detection task (a perceptual categorization/decision). It contains within-task contrasts (animal > non-animal) and interaction contrasts comparing conditions of scene complexity (high vs low), which index perceptual difficulty. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates. Thus the paper meets the fMRI during decision-making requirement, provides condition-vs-condition contrasts (including between-condition comparisons), and supplies whole-brain group-level activation maps (reported peaks). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, PET, resting-state-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore it is appropriate to include this study in the meta-analysis.

This study examines decision-making under variable outcome-precision and reports contrasts comparing precision conditions (e.g., high > low), and includes appropriate participant groups, so it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during relevant decision-making task), I5 (contrast comparing decision-making conditions), and I7 (participant groups acceptable). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are region-of-interest only (model fit over ROI; inference restricted to ROI; small-volume correction in bilateral SFC) and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps are reported. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criteria E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Additionally, there are only between-group/ROI-restricted contrasts with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect, meeting E8. Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E6 and E8. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6.

The task is social learning about an adviser’s intentions (social decision-making) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Although the study reports whole-brain group maps and coordinate tables, the reported contrasts are parametric prediction-error modulations (Outcome x low-/high-level PE) rather than decision-condition contrasts of the form required (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) applies. Inclusion criteria met: whole-brain evidence (I6), participant eligibility (I7), and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I8). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM as per review scope) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrasts such as risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, or hard>easy). Full text was available in the record provided.

This study reports task-based fMRI on a gambling (risky decision-making) task in human participants with contrasts directly comparing risk levels (e.g., high-risk wins > low-risk wins; highest odds 6/7 > lowest odds 1/7). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain and inference over whole brain for several cross-subject regressions and contrasts), and results are presented as reported peaks/tables. Participants are healthy human adults. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (risk condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported in tables/peaks) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only).

Excluded because the study’s task is sequence-prediction/statistical learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion ID E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I7 (human participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported via peak coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not clearly risky, ambiguous, or a canonical perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy is reported; the reported contrasts are omnibus within-group sequence effects). Full-text is complete in the provided record.

Exclusion E5 met: the task is social decision-making (trust/reciprocity, selecting faces/houses for smiles), which the review excludes. Exclusion E8 met: the reported neuroimaging results are exclusively between-group contrasts (PTSD vs controls) on parametric regressors (prediction error, value expectation) with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task contrasts or condition-vs-condition contrasts reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a task was conducted), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps were fitted and inferenced), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results/peaks reported in coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; instead analyses are between-group effects on model-derived regressors). Full-text was available in the provided record and thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

The task is a neuroeconomic, value-based buying/rejecting choice between food and trinket items, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm, so it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Although first-level models were fit over the whole brain, all reported inferences are restricted to regions of interest using small-volume correction (FWE-SVC), meaning no unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported; this fails I6 and meets exclusion E6. Participant eligibility is fine (healthy adult males, n=32), so I7 is satisfied. Therefore the study is excluded for E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and E6 (ROI-only reported inferences).

Excluded because the reported fMRI task (visual food perception with target-detection) is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (E5). The fMRI results are reported only within a region-of-interest (small-volume correction) rather than as a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map, violating whole-brain evidence requirement (E6). The paper reports between-group/interactions for the task without an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect (E8). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no decision-making contrasts as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level task activation map). Full text appears complete and accessible.

The study reports an fMRI (BOLD) experiment in healthy human participants performing a Trust Game decision task (n=28). It includes a within-subject contrast 'trust > safe option', which matches the meta-analysis template form for risky decision-making contrasts (risky > safe). Models were fit over the whole brain and reported group-level peaks (voxelwise whole-brain results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported as coordinate peaks. Although trust is social, here it operationalizes uncertainty about another's actions (betrayal risk), so it qualifies under the risky-DM criterion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, connectivity-only, contrasts vs baseline only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the task is a visuomotor finger-tapping/choice task analyzing entropy and surprise in stimulus/action sequences rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (results reported in acceptable formats). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrasts matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study reports a human fMRI task in which participants made old/new recognition decisions under manipulated uncertainty (decide whether an object was seen previously), satisfying I4. The reported contrasts compare uncertain versus certain conditions (UNC > CNC, UNC > CFC), matching the ambiguous decision-making contrast form (high uncertainty > low certainty) required by I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects second-level maps with reported peak coordinates (Talairach) and FDR correction, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not baseline only), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and this is an empirical fMRI activation study (not PET, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (50/50 monetary gambles) and tests a within-subject contrast comparing two decision-making conditions (CONTINGENT > RANDOM). The reported analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (fMRI during risky DM; a decision-condition vs decision-condition contrast; whole-brain group-level results; eligible participant group) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not baseline-only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and empirical).

The study investigates perception of magic tricks (causal-violation, cognitive-control) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It does not report contrasts that correspond to risky-DM, ambiguous-DM, or perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy young adults) and I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts vs control or between decision conditions), and I6 (no clear qualifying whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map for relevant decision contrasts; many reported analyses are ROI-based). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text is available in the provided record.

The task is a causal learning task (judging causal confounding), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task required by the review. Reported whole-brain, within-group parametric modulation contrasts (uncertainty, prediction strength, surprise) do not match the admitted decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 while meeting I6, I7, and I8. Exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) applies.
